title.rendered: Mac processor history: How Apple transformed computing

content.rendered:
When you think of a Mac today, you probably imagine a fast, powerful machine powered by Apple’s latest M6 chip, Apple’s first 2-nanometer processor, which now ships in the Mac mini, iMac, and 14-inch MacBook Pro. But Macs weren’t always this advanced. Their journey began in 1984 with the Motorola 68K series, a much simpler processor. Over the years, Apple transitioned to PowerPC, then Intel, and finally its own Apple silicon chips.

In this article, we’ll explore how Mac processors have evolved over time. You’ll see how each new chip improved speed, graphics, and memory, shaping the powerful Macs we use today.

2020–Present: Apple Silicon

On June 22, 2020, Apple CEO Tim Cook announced a two-year transition plan to move from Intel processors to Apple silicon. The goal was to create an all-Apple ecosystem by replacing Intel’s x86-64 architecture with Apple’s own ARM64-based chips.

Staying true to its timeline, Apple introduced its first Apple-designed Mac chip, M1, in November 2020. This was followed by more powerful M1 variants in 2021 and 2022. Apple then launched the M2, M3, M4, M5, and M6 chipsets, further pushing the boundaries of performance.

In March 2026, Apple also launched the $599 MacBook Neo, the first Mac sold to consumers that runs on an iPhone-class A18 Pro chip instead of an M-series chip. See how it stacks up in our MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air comparison.

Here’s a detailed table outlining the evolution of Mac processors, from the latest Apple M6 back to the M1:

M6 Chip Family: M6

M6 (August 2026)

Apple’s M6 is the company’s first chip built using a state-of-the-art 2-nanometer process, bringing major improvements in CPU, GPU, storage and AI performance. It features a 12-core CPU (2 super, 4 performance and 6 efficiency cores), delivering up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance than M5, and a 12-core GPU, with two additional cores compared with M5.

AI is one of the biggest focuses of M6. The chip features an all-new Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says delivers up to 2x the peak AI compute of the previous generation. Combined with the Neural Accelerators in the GPU, M6 is built to handle local AI workloads and next-generation Apple Intelligence features more efficiently.

Memory and storage performance have also been upgraded. Mac mini with M6 starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, while memory bandwidth reaches up to 170GB/s. Apple also claims up to 2x faster storage compared with the previous generation. If you’re weighing an upgrade, read our M6 Mac mini vs M4 Mac mini comparison.

After debuting in the Mac mini on August 25, 2026, M6 arrived in the new iMac and 14-inch MacBook Pro on October 27, 2026, with both shipping from November 6. The entry iMac uses a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU version of the chip.

M5 Chip Family: M5, M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra

M5 (October 2025)

The M5 is the base chip in the M5 family and is built using TSMC’s third-generation 3-nanometer process for mainstream laptops and tablets. It debuted in the 14-inch MacBook Pro and is the first Apple silicon chip to feature a dedicated Neural Accelerator in each GPU core, focusing on AI-driven tasks.

The chip features a 10-core CPU made up of 4 performance and 6 efficiency cores and up to a 10-core GPU, which provides solid graphics performance for tasks like photo editing and light 3D work. You can also configure it with up to 32GB of unified memory.

At launch, the M5 base model outperformed the whole M4 series in Geekbench Single-Core scores and had the highest single-core score of any Apple silicon chip. Early benchmarks even showed it nearly matching the M1 Ultra. Overall, it delivers a strong balance of performance, efficiency, and affordability for most users, and our M5 vs M4 MacBook Air comparison breaks down the real-world difference.

M5 Pro (March 2026)

The M5 Pro is designed for professionals who need more processing power than the base M5. Apple designed a new Fusion Architecture (a dual-die design) for this chip. It includes an 18-core CPU (6 super and 12 performance cores), offering up to 30% faster processing of intensive workloads. Apple describes it as having “the world’s fastest CPU core.”

The GPU scales up to 20 cores with a dedicated Neural Accelerator in each core, delivering much stronger graphics performance. One of the major improvements in the M5 Pro is higher memory bandwidth of up to 307 GB/s and up to 64GB of unified memory, enabling large projects and datasets to run smoothly without slowdowns.

M5 Max (March 2026)

The M5 Max sits at the top of the M5 laptop lineup and is built for users who need maximum performance. It is targeted at professionals working in fields such as 3D rendering, medical imaging, advanced video production, machine learning, and large-scale creative projects.

This chip features the same high-performance CPU architecture as the M5 Pro but dramatically expands the GPU capabilities. The GPU can scale up to 40 cores, making it one of the most powerful graphics systems available in a laptop.

The M5 Max also offers up to 614GBps memory bandwidth (460GBps on the 32-core GPU version) and supports up to 128GB of unified memory. So, it can run large professional projects efficiently without relying heavily on external storage. For full configurations and pricing, see our guide to the MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and M5 Max.

M5 Ultra (August 2026)

Apple’s M5 Ultra, introduced in August 2026, is designed specifically for demanding professional workflows and advanced AI workloads. The biggest change is Apple’s move to a quad-die architecture using next-generation UltraFusion technology, giving M5 Ultra the scale needed for extreme CPU, GPU and AI workloads.

You can configure it with up to a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU. For AI, Apple has added Neural Accelerators to the GPU for the first time on an Ultra chip, delivering up to 4.3x the peak AI compute performance of M3 Ultra. The chip also supports up to 512GB of unified memory and an enormous 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth.

Apple says M5 Ultra delivers up to 1.3x faster multithreaded CPU performance and up to 40 percent faster graphics performance than M3 Ultra. These improvements target workloads such as 3D rendering, video production, software development, scientific computing and AI inference. Not sure if you need that much power? Our M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio comparison can help.

M4 Chip family: M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max

Apple’s M4 chip family brought major advancements in silicon technology, delivering enhanced performance and efficiency across various devices. Each chip (M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max) is designed to meet different user needs.

M4 (May 2024)

The standard M4 chip is built using second-generation 3-nanometer technology, enhancing power efficiency and performance. It features a 10-core CPU with four performance cores and six efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times faster performance than the M1 chip.

The 10-core GPU provides graphics performance up to twice as fast as the M1, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 38 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks and features like Apple Intelligence.

M4 Pro (October 2024)

The M4 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 14-core CPU, comprising ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, offering up to 1.9 times faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU includes up to 20 cores, providing graphics performance twice that of the standard M4. This makes it ideal for professionals engaged in tasks like app development, video editing, and complex simulations.

M4 Max (October 2024)

The M4 Max chip is the most powerful in the M4 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features up to a 16-core CPU with 12 performance cores and four efficiency cores.

Its GPU scales up to 40 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M4 Max also supports higher unified memory bandwidth, enhancing data-intensive operations.

All M4 chips support advanced features like hardware-accelerated ray tracing and mesh shading, enhancing graphics rendering and gaming experiences. The M4 Pro and M4 Max also enable Thunderbolt 5 connectivity, offering faster data transfer speeds and improved peripheral support.

M3 Chip Family: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra

Apple’s M3 chipset family includes four powerful processors: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra. Each is designed to meet different performance needs, from everyday tasks to demanding professional workloads.

M3 (October 2023)

The M3 chip is built using advanced 3-nanometer technology, making it faster and more efficient. It features an 8-core CPU with four performance cores and four efficiency cores, delivering up to 30% faster performance than the M1.

The up-to-10-core GPU provides enhanced graphics performance, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 18 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks.

M3 Pro (October 2023)

The M3 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 12-core CPU, comprising six performance cores and six efficiency cores, offering up to 40% faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU features up to 18 cores, delivering graphics performance ideal for professionals in video editing, programming, and other demanding tasks. Apple has also integrated 37 billion transistors to enhance the overall performance of Mac machines.

M3 Max (October 2023)

The M3 Max chip is the most powerful laptop chip in the M3 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features up to a 16-core CPU with 12 performance cores and four efficiency cores.

Its GPU scales up to 40 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M3 Max also has 92 billion transistors to enhance data-intensive operations.

M3 Ultra (March 2025)

The M3 Ultra chip was Apple’s most powerful processor at launch. It features a 32-core CPU with 24 performance cores and eight efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times the performance of the M1 Ultra.

Its GPU includes up to 80 cores, providing up to 2.6 times faster graphics performance than the M1 Ultra. The M3 Ultra also supports up to 512GB of unified memory, the highest ever in a personal computer at the time, making it ideal for tasks like visual effects and AI development.

M2 Chip Family: M2, M2 Pro, M2 Max, and M2 Ultra

M2 (June 2022)

The M2 processor in the MacBook houses an 8-core CPU with a configuration of 4 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores. Apple claims that M2’s CPU delivers nearly twice the performance of the latest 10-core PC laptop processor at the same power level.

In addition, the M2 processor offers excellent work performance with an 8- or 10-core GPU, 16-core Neural Engine, and 100GBps bandwidth. M2 chips come in different RAM variations: 8GB, 16GB, and 24GB.

M2 Pro (January 2023) 

M2 Pro has a robust 10-core or 12-core CPU, including 6 or 8 performance and 4 efficiency cores. Like the M1 Pro, the M2 Pro has a built-in media engine that accelerates H.264, HEVC, and ProRes video encoding and decoding. Besides, the chip provides improved power efficiency when playing 4K and 8K ProRes streams thanks to the 16- or 19-core GPU.

Further, the M2 Pro has a 16-core Neural Engine, 200GBps memory bandwidth, and 16GB or 32GB RAM variants. Apple claimed the M2 Pro offered exceptional image processing capabilities. It was available in the MacBook Pro and Mac mini.

M2 Max (January 2023) 

M2 Max added another layer of efficiency to the Apple silicon range. Its core specifications included a 12-core CPU with 8 performance and 4 efficiency cores. Like its predecessor, the M2 Max comes with two ProRes and video-encoding engines.

Regarding graphics, it supports a 30- or 38-core GPU to give you the most detailed output. While the GPU support is better than M1 Max, the 16-core Neural Engine remains the same for both variants. In addition, Apple introduced the chip in three RAM variants: 32GB, 64GB, and 96GB.

Moreover, Apple asserted that the M2 Max was 30% faster than the M1 version when color grading in DaVinci Resolve. It also offers 400GB/s of memory bandwidth, ensuring quick processing.

M2 Ultra (June 2023) 

At WWDC 2023, Apple launched its most efficient iteration of the Apple silicon series at the time: M2 Ultra. It offers the power of two M2 Max chips connected using the robust UltraFusion architecture. Regarding specifications, M2 Ultra features a 24-core CPU and up to a 76-core GPU.

It also carries 134 billion transistors, up to 192GB of unified memory, and an impressive 800GB/s of memory bandwidth. It powered the 2023 Mac Studio and Mac Pro (here’s how the M2 Ultra Mac Studio compares with the Mac Pro); Apple discontinued the Mac Pro in March 2026. According to Apple, Mac Studio with M2 Ultra is up to 3x faster than its earlier version.

Besides, it can play 22 streams of 8K ProRes video together. The M2 Ultra chip enables the Mac Pro to deliver 3D simulations and video transcoding up to 3x faster. Moreover, the processor can simultaneously handle 24 streams of 4K camera input and encode them to ProRes.

M1 Chip family: M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, and M1 Ultra

M1 (November 2020)

The M1 processor was Apple’s first venture into chip design for the Mac. Indeed, it was a big blow for Intel! Regarding specs, M1 chips offer an 8-core CPU with 4 performance and 4 efficiency cores and a 7- or 8-core GPU.

Besides, the 16-core Neural Engine embedded in the M1 accelerates and optimizes machine learning operations on Mac. In addition, the chip offered 68.25GB/s of memory bandwidth. However, it only supported two RAM variations: 8GB and 16GB. The limited memory options didn’t go down well with many Mac users.

M1 Pro (October 2021)

Next in line in the M1 series was M1 Pro. This chipset supported 8- or 10-core CPUs, configured as 6 or 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores. Besides, Apple included a 14- or 16-core GPU, which is 2x faster than M1. Also, the new GPU was up to 7x faster than the integrated graphics on the latest 8-core PC laptop chip.

Besides, it featured a ProRes accelerator in the media engine for faster video processing. Its memory bandwidth of up to 200GB/s is nearly 3x better than the M1. This time, Apple expanded the memory options, offering 16GB and 32GB configurations.

M1 Max (October 2021)

The M1 Max and M1 Pro chips were launched together. The M1 Max had a 10-core CPU with 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores, a 24- or 32-core GPU, and a 16-core Neural Engine. The graphics performance of the 32-core GPU is up to 4x faster than that of the M1 chip.

Its two ProRes accelerators can deliver up to 2x faster video encoding than M1 Pro. Moreover, the processor offers up to 400GB/s of memory bandwidth, two times more than the M1 Pro and 6x more than the M1. Besides, the 64GB RAM option adds some extra credit points.

Apple introduced the M1 Max chip only for the MacBook Pro and Mac Studio.

M1 Ultra (March 2022)

The M1 Ultra was launched as an option for the Mac Studio. This powerful processor uses UltraFusion architecture to connect two M1 Max chips. It houses a 20-core CPU with 16 performance and 4 efficiency cores. For graphics, Apple added a massive 48- or 64-core GPU.

So, you get low latency, massive bandwidth, and better power efficiency. Furthermore, the chip has up to 128GB of unified memory built in, offering twice the media engine performance of the M1 Max.

2006-2020: Intel x86

At WWDC 2005, Apple announced its transition to Intel chips, and the first Intel Macs were announced in January 2006. These included an iMac and the MacBook Pro, which boasted up to four-fold enhanced performance over their predecessors.

Further, from Mac OS X 10.4.4, Apple included an advanced translation technology called Rosetta. It helped maintain software compatibility between generations. Soon, Apple introduced programs with universal binaries that could run on both PowerPC and Intel Macs.

As the transition to x86 came full circle, Rosetta was removed from Mac OS X 10.7 Lion going forward. So far, about 80 Mac models have featured Intel CPUs. This changed with the introduction of ARM-based Macs. Apple has confirmed that macOS Tahoe 26 is the last macOS release to support Intel Macs, so macOS 27 Golden Gate runs only on Apple silicon Macs. Apple now also lets Mac App Store apps drop Intel support.

1994-2005: Power PC

In the late 1980s, new trends began taking over the computing industry, overshadowing the legacy CPU architectures. Apple partnered with IBM and Motorola to design a common CPU platform that could rival the “Wintel” (Microsoft-Intel) domination. 

The Power Macintosh 6100 used the PowerPC architecture, following which around 87 different Mac models were launched. Clock speeds increased from 60 MHz to 2.7 GHz, which was remarkable for that era. The final Apple PowerPC model was released in November 2005. 

1984-1995: Motorola 68 K 

The 1984 Apple Macintosh computer had an 8 MHz Motorola 68000 CPU. While in development, an early Mac prototype used an 8/16-bit Motorola 6809 CPU. But after a designer noticed the impressive graphics routines that were being created for the 68000-based Apple Lisa, the more expensive 16/32-bit 68000 was chosen. 

While the Apple Lisa used only a 5 MHz 68000, the new Mac prototype could run at 8 MHz. This appealed to Steve Jobs, who was eager to upstage the Lisa team. 

Over the following decade, every Macintosh used the 68000 or its successors, including the pure 32-bit 68020, 68030, and 68040 chips. These got faster and more complex over time. Overall, at least 72 different Macs used 68K CPUs, the last of which was the PowerBook 190 in 1995.

The best is yet to come! 

The history of Apple processors beautifully captures the tech giant’s true ideology. The Mac has witnessed changes in everything from laptop size to its architecture. And with Apple’s “Pro and Tell” event on October 28, the next chapter may already be here. I hope you enjoyed reading this article as much as we enjoyed traveling the Mac timeline while penning it.

Please share your reviews in the comments section. Till then, enjoy reading.

FAQs

What is the oldest Mac software?

The oldest Mac operating system is System 1, which shipped with the original Macintosh in 1984.

What is the full form of Mac?

The full form of Mac is Macintosh.

title.rendered: Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro is here: Specs, features, and price

content.rendered:
Apple has finally done what Mac users have been waiting years for: the MacBook Pro now has a touchscreen. Announced at the “Pro and Tell” special event on October 28, the all-new MacBook Pro introduces a tandem OLED display, a Dynamic Island, a glowing Apple logo, and a thinner, lighter design. It also brings touch-based controls to macOS for the first time.

But there’s a catch. The redesigned 14-inch MacBook Pro starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch model starts at $3,399. So Apple is clearly positioning these laptops as premium machines for professionals. Pre-orders opened on October 28, 2026, and the first units arrive on Friday, November 6.

Meet the new touchscreen MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display

The biggest upgrade is Apple’s new PROLED XDR display, which replaces the previous MacBook Pro’s mini-LED technology with a tandem OLED panel. See how PROLED XDR compares with mini-LED.

Apple says the display combines advanced tandem OLED technology, sophisticated display-engine algorithms, and factory calibration to deliver “exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors.”

Here are the key display specifications:

  • Tandem OLED technology: Delivers deep blacks, rich colors, and exceptional contrast.
  • Up to 2,000 nits of peak HDR and SDR brightness: Helps keep content visible in demanding lighting conditions.
  • 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio: Improves the distinction between bright highlights and dark shadows.
  • 10Hz to 120Hz variable refresh rate: Makes scrolling, animations, and supported creative workflows feel smoother.
  • P3 and Adobe RGB color spaces: Supports color-critical work across photography, HDR video, and print design.
  • Optional nano-texture glass: Reduces reflections and glare, with the nano-texture precisely etched into the cover glass.

These features back Apple’s claim that the new MacBook Pro has the “world’s best display in a pro laptop.”

The first touchscreen Mac changes how you use macOS

For years, Apple has kept touch input on the iPhone and iPad while relying on a keyboard, trackpad, and mouse for the Mac. That changes with the new MacBook Pro.

Apple has integrated the touch sensor directly into the display panel, which the company says helps reduce latency. macOS 27 automatically translates touches into clicks, so existing apps work without needing to be updated first.

Here are some of the new touch interactions:

  • Swipe naturally through webpages and other content.
  • Pinch to zoom into photos and images.
  • Drag and drop slides between presentations.
  • Double-tap a window to fill the screen.
  • Flick a window into position to tile it.
  • Draw and manipulate designs directly on the display.

Apple has also redesigned the laptop’s hinge to support touchscreen use, helping keep the display stable when users tap and swipe.

Dynamic Island replaces the notch

Another major design change is the removal of the familiar MacBook Pro notch.

Apple has introduced a smaller Dynamic Island that brings an iPhone-inspired interface to the Mac. It serves as a central place to access Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Users can search their Mac, ask questions, check ongoing activities, and control music from this interactive area.

The change also gives the redesigned laptop a more modern appearance, with the Dynamic Island taking up less space than the previous notch.

A thinner, lighter design with a glowing Apple logo

Apple has redesigned the MacBook Pro’s chassis to make it more portable without compromising its professional capabilities. Apple says the 16-inch model is nearly 1mm thinner than the existing design, and the 14-inch model is about half a millimeter thinner.

The new 14-inch model weighs just 3 pounds, while the 16-inch version weighs 4 pounds. Apple says those figures represent reductions of half a pound and 0.7 pounds, respectively, compared with their predecessors.

The redesigned laptop also brings back the glowing Apple logo, a feature that many MacBook fans will remember from older models.

Apple has updated the audio system, too. The laptop features six speakers, an all-new woofer design, and updated tweeters. The company says the system delivers 50% deeper bass and clearer sound.

M5 Pro and M5 Max power the new MacBook Pro

Despite the extensive redesign, Apple hasn’t introduced a new processor generation for these models. The new MacBook Pro uses the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, which Apple describes as its most powerful chips built for a professional laptop. Apple’s newer M6 chip is instead going into the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the iMac with M6 chip, neither of which has a touchscreen.

The available configurations support:

  • Up to 128GB of unified memory (M5 Max; up to 64GB with M5 Pro).
  • Up to 16TB of storage (M5 Max).
  • Hardware and software capabilities designed for demanding professional and AI workloads.

The combination of Apple silicon, unified memory, and macOS 27 is designed to handle complex projects, including video editing, graphics work, development, and machine-learning tasks.

Connectivity, camera, audio, and battery life

The redesigned MacBook Pro includes a broad range of hardware features for professionals who need to connect accessories and work away from a desk.

Here’s what else Apple has confirmed:

  • Battery life: Up to 24 hours on the 16-inch M5 Pro model (up to 22 hours on the 14-inch M5 Pro model), according to Apple.
  • Camera: A 12MP Center Stage camera.
  • Microphones: Studio-quality microphones.
  • Ports: Three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe charging, and a headphone jack.
  • Wireless connectivity: Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, powered by Apple’s N1 wireless chip.
  • Security: Touch ID for convenient and secure authentication.
  • External displays: Up to three with M5 Pro and up to four with M5 Max.

This feature set is particularly useful for photographers, video editors, and other professionals who regularly connect external storage, cameras, and displays.

MacBook Pro price and availability

The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, with M5 Pro and M5 Max configurations. Buyers can choose Silver or Space Black finishes, with standard or nano-texture display configurations.

Here’s the full US starting-price breakdown:

Apple also lists education pricing of $2,749 for the 14-inch M5 Pro model, $3,199 for the 16-inch M5 Pro model, $4,199 for the 14-inch M5 Max model, and $4,499 for the 16-inch M5 Max model. Opting for nano-texture glass adds $150 in the US.

Pre-orders opened on October 28, 2026, and the new MacBook Pro is scheduled to begin arriving to customers, and in Apple Store locations and authorized resellers, on Friday, November 6.

Unlock more with Apple:

  • AirPods 5 Wireless Earbuds
  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

title.rendered: 10 best ChatGPT alternatives in 2026 (free and paid)

content.rendered:
ChatGPT is great, and it now gives even free users unlimited text chats. Still, some jobs are much better done with another AI model. We’ve been testing AI tools constantly for the last four years, and this list collects the alternatives worth trying.

The list is ordered by use case, not by overall performance, so you can pick the one that fits what you actually do. Most have a free tier, so you can try the part that matters to you before paying for another subscription.

ChatGPT alternatives compared: free tiers and prices

Prices below are standard US monthly web prices at the time of writing. We’ll keep this article updated, but some details can change quickly in this space.

1. Claude: My pick for writing and coding

Claude is the first alternative I’d try if ChatGPT keeps sanding your writing into the same smooth, generic voice. Claude is also currently a bit better at coding than ChatGPT’s Codex, if you’re into that. But the main reason to use Claude is that it has a better sense of what you’re asking and makes slightly fewer hallucination mistakes.

You also lose very little in the switch, because Claude has a good range of connectors and features like artifacts. However, it can’t generate images, and top-tier models like Fable are only included on Max plans; Pro users have to pay for them through usage credits. So if you want to stick to a $20 Pro plan, ChatGPT may still have an edge here.

Pro costs $20 a month or $200 billed annually. It raises your allowance, but paid access still has caps, and long chats or large attachments use up more of it. Upgrade when the free limits start interrupting your work, rather than expecting Pro to mean unlimited.

If you’re still deciding between the two, our ChatGPT vs. Claude comparison breaks down how they differ in writing, coding, and everyday use, so you can decide which one fits your workflow better. If you’re new to Claude, our guide to Claude’s icons and symbols explains what its buttons and controls do.

Try Claude

2. Meta AI / Muse: Help where you’re already chatting

Meta AI’s appeal is convenience. If you spend your day in WhatsApp or Instagram, asking for a gift idea there is easier than opening another app. Everyday use remains free, while Meta One Core starts at $7.99 a month for more AI creation and app perks.

Muse is Meta’s separate personal agent. It can work across connected services and take actions, with approval for sensitive steps such as sending an email. It has a limited free allowance and separate subscriptions starting with Power at $20 a month. So if you use ChatGPT’s dots, Muse gives you an alternative agent.

However, the major limitation with Meta is the model itself. While it’s impressive and has improved a lot, it’s a smaller model at the end of the day compared to models like OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra.

Muse is worth considering if you want help carrying out personal tasks, but it’s only available in the US and Canada for now. Give it one small task you can check before connecting more services. A chatbot suggesting a reply and an agent sending one need different levels of trust.

Try Meta AI or try Muse.

You can also use Muse from your wrist: its Apple Watch app supports text, dictation, and calls. See how Meta Muse works on Apple Watch.

3. Microsoft Copilot: An easy start for Windows users

Copilot is an easy place to start if you already use Microsoft’s apps. Its free chat handles everyday jobs such as rewriting an awkward email or explaining a spreadsheet formula. Web and mobile apps mean you don’t need a Windows PC, though Windows and Microsoft 365 users have the clearest reason to pick it.

Working inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Outlook is where a subscription becomes useful. Microsoft 365 Personal costs $9.99 a month and includes Copilot in those apps. Premium costs $19.99 and adds more usage and exclusive features. Check what you already pay for before upgrading.

The catch is that free Copilot chat doesn’t include the same access inside Microsoft 365. If you only need a few answers and email rewrites, paying for the Office integration may buy you very little.

Try Microsoft Copilot

4. DeepSeek: A free second opinion on a hard problem

DeepSeek is worth trying for a math problem or a spreadsheet formula that keeps returning the wrong number. Students and anyone looking for another approach to a problem can use its reasoning and web search without buying a subscription. The consumer app and web chat are free; developer API billing is separate.

The trade-off is data handling. DeepSeek processes and stores personal data in China, and its policy allows data use to improve its models. Use a made-up spreadsheet example instead of your employer’s file. You can fix the formula without sharing the real figures. We’ve already covered DeepSeek vs. ChatGPT on iPhone, so you can check that comparison in detail.

Try DeepSeek

5. Duck.ai: Quick questions without an account

Duck.ai is the one I’d suggest to someone whose first question is, “Do I have to sign up?” You can choose a model and chat for free without an account. DuckDuckGo removes identifying metadata before forwarding requests, and its provider agreements prohibit using those chats for model training. That makes it a useful option for occasional questions you don’t want attached to a chatbot account.

The free version has a daily cap, so long work sessions can hit a wall. In supported countries, DuckDuckGo Plus costs $9.99 a month and Pro costs $19.99, bundling more AI access with other privacy services. I’d pay for the bundle only if you’ll also use its VPN or other included services.

Your prompts still go to a model provider. Recent chats stay on your device by default, with optional encrypted Sync & Backup for other devices.

Try Duck.ai

6. Mistral Vibe: The assistant formerly called Le Chat

If you remember Le Chat, this is the same service under its newer Vibe name. Mistral has added work and coding modes, but the conversational Chat mode remains. It’s a useful general assistant to try if you’d prefer France-based Mistral over another major US platform.

The free plan includes limited messages, web search, document uploads, and basic image generation and editing. Start with an ordinary document task, such as pulling deadlines out of a club newsletter, before connecting your apps.

Pro costs $14.99 a month, excluding taxes, and gives you more room to work. It undercuts Claude and Perplexity, but a lower price only matters if you like the answers. Messages, searches, and uploads still have plan limits, with fair-use restrictions on paid access too.

Try Mistral Vibe

7. Perplexity: Research you can follow back to a source

Perplexity searches the web and puts citations alongside its answers. Use it to compare subscription plans or find the origin of a statistic, then open the relevant source. Students, researchers, and anyone gathering facts before a decision get somewhere to check the answer.

Core search and chat are free, with limits on advanced features. Pro costs $20 a month or $200 billed annually and makes sense when deeper research and file work become regular needs.

A citation can still fail to support the exact claim beside it. Check the source behind the detail that changes your decision, such as a product’s compatibility requirement. Perplexity saves you the hunt for pages; you still need to read the relevant bit.

Try Perplexity

8. Gemini: The practical pick for Google users

Gemini makes more sense if your email and documents already live in Google. Summarizing a thread inside Gmail saves copying it into another chatbot. The paid plans bundle storage too, so check whether an AI plan could replace your existing storage subscription.

The free version offers everyday chat, Gemini Live, image tools, and limited research features, with Flash-Lite listed on the current US plan. Google AI Plus costs $4.99 a month, while AI Pro costs $19.99 and includes stronger models, higher limits, and Gemini in Docs and other apps.

Choose carefully if you’re paying for a particular model. Following Google’s October changes to Gemini access, free and entry-level plans have a narrower selection. AI Plus won’t give you everything in Pro. The higher tier earns its price when you’ll use both the stronger models and the app integration.

Try Gemini

9. Grok: Useful when the conversation is happening on X

Grok can search both the web and posts on X. That helps when you want reactions to a product launch or the original post behind a claim being passed around. If you regularly follow discussions and breaking developments on X, that connection matters more than its chatbot personality.

Free access includes limited chat. For new customers, X Subscription Plus costs $8 a month and Premium costs $30, with paid plans bundling Grok, X, and Cursor access. Existing SuperGrok plans can continue, so check your subscriptions before adding another one.

Finding a claim on X doesn’t establish that it’s true. Ask for the original post and separate it from what other accounts are repeating. A busy discussion can tell you what people think without proving what happened.

Try Grok

10. Kagi Assistant: Worth a look if you’re paying for search

Kagi combines a paid, ad-free search engine with an AI assistant. It’s most appealing if you want both in one subscription, since you’re deciding whether to replace your search engine as well as where to ask AI questions.

There’s a free trial with 100 searches and 100 Assistant interactions. After that, Starter costs $5 a month for 300 searches and Quick-mode Assistant access. Professional costs $10, removes the search cap, and increases the Assistant allowance.

The catch is that Research mode and flagship model selection require the $25 Ultimate plan, still subject to fair use. Spend the trial on questions you normally search for. If those results don’t earn your money, the bundled assistant is a weak reason to keep paying.

Try Kagi Assistant

Honorable mentions: Brave Leo and Poe

These two make more sense for a particular habit than as the first replacement for everyone.

Brave Leo

Leo works inside the Brave browser and can summarize the page or PDF you’re reading. There’s a free version, and Leo Premium costs $14.99 a month. Try it if you already use Brave and keep copying text into another chatbot. Its browser focus is also a reason to skip it if you’re happy elsewhere.

Try Brave Leo

Poe

Poe puts multiple AI models in one app, with free access and paid plans that add points and model options. It suits people who want to compare models without maintaining several separate subscriptions. Each bot has its own point cost, though, so check how much your preferred model uses before subscribing.

Try Poe

Which ChatGPT alternative should you choose?

I’d start with Claude if writing and editing take up most of your AI use, or Perplexity if you spend more time finding facts and checking sources. If your main frustration is copying work between apps, Gemini or Copilot may be the more useful switch, depending on whether you use Google or Microsoft tools.

For occasional questions, try a free option before adding another subscription. Duck.ai is an easy starting point if you don’t want an account, while DeepSeek is worth trying for non-sensitive problems you want help working through.

Pick the two that fit your routine and give them the same real task. Keep the one that needs less correcting, and pay only when its free limits regularly get in your way.

title.rendered: Cat Battles codes (November 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Cat Battles Codes on November 01, 2026

Roblox is packed with all kinds of wacky games, but Cat Battles is one you shouldn’t miss. In this physics-based arena brawler, you control a cat and battle other players by punching, grabbing, kicking, and tossing them out of the ring. Your goal is simple: be the last cat standing.

Winning isn’t just about throwing punches, though. You’ll need to use your abilities strategically and earn Coins to unlock cosmetic rewards and customize your cat. That’s where Cat Battles codes come in handy! Redeem them for free Coins and get more opportunities to collect furs, gear, and emotes.

All working Cat Battles codes

  • YARNZ2K: 250 Coins (NEW)
  • 1KCHONKY: 250 Coins (NEW)
  • CATS: 150 Coins
  • NEWGAME: 250 Coins
  • RELEASE: 250 Coins

As of now, these are the only active Cat Battles codes available. Make sure to redeem them as soon as possible, as codes can expire without warning, leaving you unable to claim their rewards.

Expired Cat Battles codes

Currently, all available codes are valid and can be redeemed. Keep in mind that developers may remove them when new codes are issued, so it’s best to redeem them promptly.

How to redeem Cat Battles codes in Roblox

Now that you have the codes, here’s how to redeem them and claim your rewards.

  1. Fire up Cat Battles on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load and complete the short tutorial.
  3. Click on the gear icon.
  4. Paste a working code and hit Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the codes, the rewards should be added to your inventory automatically.

Why aren’t my Cat Battles codes working?

Are your Cat Battles codes not working? Well, double-check that you’ve entered them exactly as listed above. Keep in mind that these codes are case-sensitive, so make sure there are no extra spaces before or after them.

You can simply copy and paste the codes directly from our list. If a code still doesn’t work, it might have expired, or you may have already redeemed its rewards.

How to get more Cat Battles codes

The developers don’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new Cat Battles codes. Most codes are released to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, bug fixes, or community milestones.

title.rendered: Gemini Notebook adds built-in audio recorder to Android and iOS apps

content.rendered:
Google is making it easier to record lectures, meetings, and voice notes with a new built-in audio recorder for its Gemini Notebook apps on Android and iOS. The feature, now widely rolling out as of October 27, 2026, lets users capture audio directly in the app and save recordings alongside other research materials. So you don’t need to switch between separate recording and note-taking apps.

Gemini Notebook gets a dedicated audio recorder

The new recorder appears as a microphone icon at the bottom of the Gemini Notebook app, positioned between the camera and Create New floating action buttons.

Users can tap the microphone to start recording audio. Starting a recording from the home screen creates a new notebook, while recording from the Sources tab saves the audio to an existing notebook.

This makes it easier to organize recordings by subject, project, or research topic. Students can record lectures, professionals can capture meeting discussions, and users can save spoken ideas for later reference.

Record audio in the background for up to one hour

Gemini Notebook’s recording interface includes pause and finish controls, along with a waveform animation and a timer to show recording progress.

One particularly useful addition is support for background recording. Users can switch to another app or lock their phone’s screen without interrupting an active recording.

However, each recording session is limited to one hour. After recording finishes, the audio uploads to Gemini Notebook and becomes part of the notebook’s source materials.

Notebook creation gets a small Improvement

Google has also simplified the notebook creation process. Tapping the floating Create New button now immediately starts a new notebook instead of opening a panel for adding a source.

The update complements Gemini Notebook’s existing AI-powered research and learning tools, helping users manage information without constantly switching between apps.

How to get the audio recorder

To use the recording feature, open the Gemini Notebook app on your phone and look for the microphone icon near the bottom of the screen.

Tap it to start recording, then tap the checkmark when you’re done to finish the session. The recording is saved as a source in your notebook, where you can chat with it, cite it, and keep building your research by adding other sources.

Google first announced the feature on September 15, 2026, and it is now widely rolling out to mobile users. The initial rollout covers users who have English set as their output language. If the microphone icon is missing, try force-stopping and reopening the app, although availability may vary during the rollout.

Overall, the built-in recorder makes Gemini Notebook a more practical tool for students, researchers, and professionals who want to keep audio recordings and research materials together.

Update: Verified the latest Hollow Codes on November 20, 2026

Are you a fan of the anime Bleach? If so, you should give Hollow a try! In this Roblox action RPG, you can choose between a Hollow, Soul Reaper, or Arrancar and embark on quests, fight enemies and bosses, and unlock powerful skills and weapons as you work your way up.

However, becoming the strongest fighter isn’t easy. You’ll need the right abilities and character build to gain an edge over your opponents. That’s where Hollow codes come in handy! Redeem them for free rerolls and EXP boosts to customize your character and speed up your progression.

All working Hollow codes

None

As of now, these are the only active Hollow codes available. Make sure to redeem them as soon as possible, as codes can expire without warning, leaving you unable to claim their rewards.

Expired Hollow codes

SORRYFORDELAY

How to redeem Hollow codes in Roblox

Once you’ve picked the codes you want to use, follow these steps to claim your free Coins.

  1. Fire up Hollow on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load and complete the short tutorial.
  3. Click on the gamepad icon to open the menu.
  4. Choose the Codes section.
  5. Paste a working code and hit Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the codes, the rewards should be added to your inventory automatically.

Why aren’t my Hollow codes working?

If your Hollow codes aren’t working, double-check that you’ve entered them exactly as listed above. Keep in mind that these codes are case-sensitive, so make sure there are no extra spaces before or after them.

You can simply copy and paste the codes directly from our list. If a code still doesn’t work, it might have expired, or you may have already redeemed its rewards.

How to get more Hollow codes

The developers don’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new Hollow codes. Most codes are released to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, bug fixes, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Discord server: Visit the Hollow Discord server to find announcements and newly released codes.
  • Follow the Roblox game page: Check the game’s official Roblox page and community for updates, announcements, and potential code releases.
  • Bookmark this page: We’ll update this guide whenever new Hollow codes become available, so you can easily find the latest rewards in one place.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Above The Rim codes, Anime Ball Duels codes, and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

How do you get free rewards in Hollow?

You can earn free rewards in Hollow by progressing through the game and completing tasks. However, the easiest method to get rewards is by redeeming codes for free rerolls and XP boosts.

What are the races in Hollow?

HOLLOW features three main paths: Hollow, Soul Reaper, and Arrancar. Each offers different progression options and abilities, allowing you to develop a character that suits your preferred playstyle.

How do you level up quickly in Hollow?

The best way to level up in Hollow is by completing missions, defeating NPC enemies, and using EXP boosts whenever it is possible.

title.rendered: iPhone 18e leak reveals two major upgrades, but keeps a 60Hz display

content.rendered:
Apple’s upcoming iPhone 18e could bring two significant upgrades: a faster A20 chip and a potentially improved selfie camera. However, the same leak suggests the budget-friendly iPhone may retain its 60Hz display and single rear camera.

A recent Weibo post from leaker Digital Chat Station shared early details about Apple’s next entry-level iPhone, expected in spring 2027 alongside the rumored iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2. Apple has not officially confirmed the device or its specifications.

iPhone 18e could feature Apple’s A20 chip

One of the biggest rumored upgrades is Apple’s A20 processor. The iPhone 18e could move from the iPhone 17e’s 3nm A19 chip to the next-generation A20, potentially bringing it in line with the upcoming standard iPhone 18.

The A20 is expected to use a 2-nanometer manufacturing process. So far, the A20 family has only appeared as the A20 Pro in the iPhone 18 Pro models, so it would be a significant performance leap for Apple’s budget iPhone if accurate.

Front camera upgrade could improve selfies

The leak also points to a possible front-camera upgrade. The iPhone 18e could feature a 24-megapixel selfie camera, compared with the 12-megapixel camera on the iPhone 17e.

A higher-resolution camera could capture more detail in selfies and offer greater flexibility when cropping photos. However, it’s unclear whether the leaker is referring to a new sensor or mistakenly to the 18MP Center Stage camera used in the iPhone 17 lineup. Either way, it would be an upgrade over the iPhone 17e.

60Hz display and single rear camera may remain

Despite these potential improvements, the iPhone 18e could retain a 6.12-inch OLED display with LTPS technology and a 60Hz refresh rate.

This means users may not get the smoother scrolling and animations available on iPhones with 120Hz ProMotion displays. The phone is also expected to keep a single 48-megapixel rear camera and other specs similar to its predecessor. Separately, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo has reported that the iPhone 18e could get 9GB of RAM, up from 8GB on the iPhone 17e.

iPhone 18e release date: What to expect

Apple could launch the iPhone 18e in spring 2027 as part of its reportedly revised iPhone release schedule. There is no official information on pricing or the release date yet.

With memory and storage prices rising, Apple may need to balance hardware improvements against production costs. Since the iPhone 18e is intended to remain a budget-friendly option, Apple could limit upgrades compared with a typical yearly refresh to keep the price competitive.

For now, all specifications and release details remain unconfirmed until Apple makes an official announcement.

title.rendered: The Final Spritemare in Fortnite: Full schedule, boosted Sprites, and login rewards

content.rendered:
Fortnite Override and Fortnitemares 2026 have entered their final stretch. As a result, the devs have decided to give players one final push to complete their sprite collection through a series of boosted days, known together as The Final Spritemare, during which the spawn rates of certain sprites will go up.

The event runs from October 27 to October 31, 2026, with daily changes starting at 9 AM ET (6:30 PM IST). Across the five days, players can earn double Sprite XP and Sprite Dust, claim a Lucky Locator through a daily login quest, and find additional loot in chests.

With 162 Fortnite sprite entries released throughout the season, including variants, this is a valuable opportunity for completionists to fill the remaining gaps in their collections before the next Fortnite season begins.

The Final Spritemare full schedule

Here’s the complete schedule for The Final Spritemare, including each day’s boosted Sprite variants, loot-pool additions, and special rewards.

Note: The daily boosts begin at 9 AM ET / 1 PM UTC and run until the following day’s changeover.

In addition to these benefits, on the final two days of the season, you will also get a few freebies and a couple other gameplay boosts. First off, those logging in on October 30 can claim the Calaverita Sprays and an emoticon for free.

Secondly, those playing the game on October 31 are certain to find the Hunter Scavenger, Prop Hunt, and Spooky Sprinter overrides in Fortnite’s Override Consoles during their matches. Moreover, the total number of Pumpkin Chests will also be aped up on this day, further helping players grow their collection.

The Final Spritemare: Daily login rewards and boosts

Besides the rotating daily changes, The Final Spritemare includes several bonuses that remain active throughout the event. These rewards and boosts make it easier to find, collect, and master Sprites before the season ends.

Here’s what you can expect:

  1. Double Sprite XP: Earn twice the usual Sprite XP to help level up your collected Sprites.
  2. Double Sprite Dust: Collect twice the usual Sprite Dust during the event.
  3. Daily Lucky Locator: Complete the daily login quest to earn a Lucky Locator. You can claim one on each of the five event days.
  4. Extra chest loot: 1-Up Tokens and Portable Extractors may appear in chests.

These bonuses are especially useful if you’re still working toward completing your Sprite collection. The double XP and Sprite Dust boosts also help you progress toward Sprite Mastery, while Lucky Locators can help you track down Sprites you haven’t discovered yet.

If you’re missing specific variants, make the most of the daily boosts instead of relying entirely on random encounters. For example, focus on Gold and Cheat Master Sprites on October 27, Loot Hacker on October 28, Bounty Hunter on October 29, and Trick or Treat on October 30.

The event’s double Sprite XP and Sprite Dust bonuses also reduce the grind involved in progressing through Sprite Mastery. This can be particularly helpful for special variants, including Quack Sprites, which have their own collection and mastery requirements.

Countdown to Fortnite Treasure Hunters

As Fortnite Override draws to a close, the next seasonal experience is approaching. Epic Games has teased Fortnite Treasure Hunters, a new One Piece-themed mini-season scheduled to begin on November 1, 2026.

One of the biggest teasers so far is a giant treasure chest that players can find in Fortnite Battle Royale. The chest has also attracted attention for the music that plays nearby. You can read more about it in our guide to the One Piece chest location in Fortnite.

Override has focused heavily on gaming franchises, weapons, Match Overrides, and collectible Sprites. Treasure Hunters is set to shift the spotlight toward the popular One Piece anime and its pirate-adventure theme.

With the current season nearing its end, The Final Spritemare gives players one last chance to work on their Sprite collections while enjoying the event’s boosted rewards. If you’ve been putting off Sprite Mastery, use the remaining days wisely before Fortnite moves on to its next chapter.

  • How to unlock and find Finger Guns in Fortnite
  • Stalkboxes in Fortnite: What they do and how to find them
  • What is Poppy Secret Run and How can I play

  • CyberPowerPC Gaming PC (GeForce RTX 5060)

  • Ergonomic Gaming Chair (Adjustable Lumbar Support)

title.rendered: ChatGPT can now access iCloud Mail and Calendar to manage emails and events

content.rendered:
OpenAI has added iCloud Mail and Calendar integrations to ChatGPT, giving Apple users a new way to manage their emails and appointments through the AI chatbot. Announced on October 27, the integrations let users search their iCloud inboxes, catch up on messages, check upcoming events, and update calendar entries in ChatGPT.

The new integrations are available across all ChatGPT plans, including the free tier, on the web, desktop, and iOS. This lets the chatbot work with information stored in Apple’s services rather than relying entirely on what users manually provide in conversations.

OpenAI announces iCloud Mail and Calendar integrations

OpenAI announced the rollout on its official ChatGPT account on X, describing the integrations as a long-requested addition.

Much requested, and now yours to connect: iCloud Mail and Calendar plugins are available in ChatGPT. Ask ChatGPT to find that email, catch up on your inbox, check what’s next, or update a calendar event. Phew. Available on all ChatGPT plans on web, desktop, and iOS. https://t.co/g68OWoFVg8

— ChatGPT (@ChatGPT) October 27, 2026

The company confirmed availability across all ChatGPT plans on web, desktop, and iOS.

The update lets you connect your Apple email and calendar accounts to ChatGPT, which previously supported only Google and Microsoft services like Gmail and Google Calendar. OpenAI has also rolled out the Apple Messages plugin, but it’s available only in Work and Codex mode on the Mac app.

ChatGPT can search iCloud emails and manage messages

The iCloud Mail integration allows ChatGPT to search and read emails, manage messages and drafts, send emails, and look up iCloud contacts. This gives users a conversational way to retrieve information buried in their inboxes, summarize mail threads, or handle routine email tasks.

However, the integration is built specifically for iCloud Mail. It supports Apple email addresses ending in @icloud.com, @me.com, and @mac.com. Other email accounts configured in Apple’s Mail app, including Gmail and Outlook, aren’t automatically included.

iCloud Calendar integration brings scheduling to ChatGPT

The iCloud Calendar integration lets ChatGPT read scheduled events, create calendar entries, and update existing events through natural-language requests. For example, you can ask ChatGPT to check your upcoming appointments or find an available time for a meeting.

The integration also works with events displayed in the iPhone’s Calendar app, or any third-party calendar app, when they are stored in iCloud Calendar. This is useful for Apple users who manage their appointments across different apps but keep their calendar data synchronized through iCloud.

The integrations extend ChatGPT’s connected-app capabilities

The iCloud announcement also has implications for OpenAI’s broader AI assistant strategy. ChatGPT plugins allow the chatbot to use information from external services when responding to requests, making it more useful for everyday productivity tasks.

The integrations can also be used by OpenAI’s proactive AI agent, Dots, for the first time. However, that doesn’t mean every feature or agent, like Work or Codex, can use them in exactly the same way.

To connect either service, users must create an Apple app-specific password. This is separate from their regular Apple Account password. Then simply open ChatGPT, go to Settings > Plugins, and select iCloud Mail or iCloud Calendar. Otherwise, ask a ChatGPT Dot to set up the plugins. Each plugin is connected separately: Mail uses your iCloud email address, while Calendar uses your primary Apple Account email.

The rollout is notable because it includes free ChatGPT users, not just paid subscribers. That gives more Apple users access to the new capabilities without requiring an upgrade.

  • AirPods 5 Wireless Earbuds
  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

title.rendered: Apple unveils 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip and up to 24-hour battery

content.rendered:
Apple has officially introduced its new 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by the M6 chip, alongside a new M6-powered iMac. The new laptop brings faster graphics, improved AI performance, enhanced battery life, and advanced wireless capabilities.

The M6 model retains the Liquid Retina XDR display and familiar MacBook Pro design. Pre-orders open October 28, with prices starting at $1,999.

M6 chip brings faster performance and AI capabilities

At the heart of the new 14-inch MacBook Pro is Apple’s M6 chip, featuring a 12-core CPU and a 12-core GPU, two more cores each than the M5. As per Apple, the new processor is built to handle everyday tasks and demanding professional applications, such as software development, 3D rendering, and AI-powered workflows.

Compared with the M5, the M6 offers up to 30% faster graphics performance and up to 25% faster AI workloads. It also features Neural Accelerators in every GPU core and a third-generation ray-tracing engine. According to Apple, the M6 speeds up project build performance in Xcode and LLM prompt processing by up to 1.3x compared with the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5.

Apple also equipped the chip with a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, up to 1.9x faster than the M5, to support AI features across macOS. This includes running large language models locally, allowing supported AI workloads to run directly on the Mac rather than relying entirely on cloud processing.

Memory and storage get an upgrade

The 14-inch MacBook Pro comes with 16GB of unified memory as standard and is customizable to 32GB. Memory bandwidth goes up to 170GB/s, which makes it capable of running demanding applications, large projects, and multiple workloads more efficiently.

The new model starts with a 1TB SSD, double the 512GB the 14-inch M5 model offered at launch.

Familiar design with a Liquid Retina XDR display

Apple retained the 14-inch Liquid Retina XDR display, which offers high contrast, detailed visuals, and HDR support. The display reaches up to 1,600 nits of peak HDR brightness and provides a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio.

Users can also configure the MacBook Pro with an optional nano-texture display finish designed to reduce reflections in bright environments. It could be helpful for professionals who have to work under studio lights or near a window.

The laptop retains a premium aluminum body in Space Black and Silver. While the M6 brings significant internal improvements, Apple has kept the familiar design.

Connectivity, camera, and audio features

The new 14-inch MacBook Pro adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, supporting newer wireless standards when paired with compatible networks and accessories.

Physical ports include:

  • Three Thunderbolt 4 ports
  • An HDMI port
  • An SDXC card slot
  • MagSafe 3 charging
  • A headphone jack

The laptop also supports up to two external displays, making it suitable for multi-monitor workstations.

For video calls, Apple retains a 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View support. The laptop also includes a six-speaker sound system with Spatial Audio and a studio-quality three-microphone array.

These features make the MacBook Pro suitable not only for creative production and software development but also for remote meetings, presentations, and content creation.

Battery life reaches up to 24 hours

According to Apple, the new MacBook Pro can last up to 24 hours on a single charge. This is the longest battery life Apple has advertised for a Mac, though actual runtime depends on workload, settings, and configuration.

The laptop also supports fast charging. With a compatible 96W USB-C power adapter, Apple says users can charge the battery to approximately 50% in around 30 minutes.

For people who work away from a desk, the combination of improved performance per watt and long battery life could be one of the most practical benefits of the M6 upgrade.

macOS 27 and Apple Intelligence

The new MacBook Pro runs macOS 27 Golden Gate, which brings Apple’s latest software features and AI capabilities to the laptop.

Apple Intelligence and Siri AI are designed to help users work with information across supported apps, assist with writing, and perform certain tasks more efficiently. Siri AI is currently available in beta in macOS 27.2 in supported languages. The M6’s Neural Engine and GPU-based Neural Accelerators provide additional hardware support for compatible AI workloads.

The ability to run supported large language models locally may also appeal to developers and users who want to experiment with AI tools while keeping certain processing tasks on their own devices.

MacBook Pro M6 price and availability

The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 in the United States, with education pricing starting at $1,899 for eligible customers. The base configuration includes 16GB of unified memory and a 1TB SSD, while higher configurations offer up to 32GB of memory and 4TB of storage.

Pre-orders begin Wednesday, October 28, and the laptop will be available in stores and begin arriving to customers on Friday, November 6.

In India, the starting price is ₹2,39,900, with an education price of ₹2,27,900 for eligible students. Indian pre-orders also begin October 28, with availability starting November 6.

In short, the new 14-inch M6-powered MacBook Pro is a significant upgrade for current M5 MacBook Pro owners and those upgrading from older Apple Silicon Macs, especially M1. It’s ideal for college students, business users, creators, and more.

title.rendered: Apple launches new iMac with M6 chip, N1 wireless upgrades, and more

content.rendered:
Apple has refreshed its colorful all-in-one desktop with a major performance upgrade. On October 27, 2026, Apple announced a new iMac powered by its M6 chip, delivering faster performance, improved graphics, and more powerful AI capabilities.

The updated model continues Apple’s focus on combining powerful hardware with a slim design and a simple all-in-one desktop setup. It starts at $1,499, with pre-orders opening on October 28 at 10:10 a.m. PT (1:10 p.m. ET) and availability from November 6.

New iMac gets Apple’s powerful M6 chip

The biggest upgrade is Apple’s M6 chip, which improves computing and graphics performance while supporting more demanding AI workloads. Built on a 2-nm process, it features up to a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, with support for up to 32GB of unified memory and up to 170GB/s of memory bandwidth.

Compared with the M4-powered iMac, which offers up to a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, the M6 model delivers a significant performance boost. Apple claims up to 1.5x faster performance in apps like Microsoft Excel, twice as fast graphics, and 5x faster on-device AI performance.

These improvements could benefit demanding apps, video editing, and AI-powered tools. For people who have an M4 iMac, this update will be most noticeable when handling graphics- and AI-heavy tasks. Users coming from older Macs will have a better experience altogether.

Familiar all-in-one design with a 4.5K Retina display

Apple has retained the iMac’s distinctive slim design rather than introducing a dramatic redesign. It features a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display, designed to deliver sharp text, detailed images, and vibrant colors.

Apple is offering the iMac in seven colors: blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver.

The all-in-one format remains one of the iMac’s biggest advantages. Users can set up their workspace without needing a separate desktop tower and monitor, making it a convenient choice for home offices, students, and people who prefer a clean desk setup.

Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and faster SSD performance

Beyond the processor, Apple has improved connectivity and storage in the new iMac.

The M6 model includes an N1 wireless chip that supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. The 12-core models also offer optional 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet with “up to 2.5x faster wired connectivity than the previous generation” for users who prefer a wired network connection.

Apple says the new iMac also delivers up to twice as fast SSD read and write performance compared with the M4 model. Faster storage can help with file transfers, loading applications, and workflows involving large files.

These upgrades may be particularly useful for creative professionals who regularly work with large photo libraries, video projects, and other storage-intensive content.

iMac M6 price and pre-orders

The new M6-powered iMac starts at $1,499 in the US for the base configuration with a 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB of unified memory, 256GB of storage, and two Thunderbolt/USB 4 ports. Apple also offers a higher-end configuration with a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, and four Thunderbolt 4 ports, starting at $1,699.

On the 12-core model, users can choose up to 32GB of unified memory and up to 2TB of storage.

With education pricing, the two models start at $1,449 and $1,599. In India, the iMac with M6 starts at ₹1,74,900 for the 10-core model and ₹1,99,900 for the 12-core model.

Pre-orders for the new iMac begin on October 28, 2026, and it will be available from November 6, 2026, at Apple Store locations and authorized resellers.

You may like to read: What didn’t change between the M4 and M6 iMac?

Unlock more with Apple:

  • AirPods 5 Wireless Earbuds
  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

title.rendered: All GTA 6 exclusive features PS5 players can enjoy

content.rendered:
It’s hard to believe, but Grand Theft Auto 6 is now just a few weeks away from launch. After years of delays, rumors, and endless speculation, Rockstar Games is preparing to take us back to Vice City on November 19, 2026. Pre-orders are already live for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

Although GTA 6 is launching on both consoles, PlayStation has highlighted several features designed to make the experience more immersive on PS5. These include the DualSense controller’s haptic feedback and adaptive triggers, which respond to the action as Jason and Lucia explore Leonida.

So, what advantages can you expect if you’re playing GTA 6 on a PS5 or PS5 Pro? And are any of these features genuinely exclusive to Sony’s console? Here’s everything we know so far.

GTA 6 PS5 features at a glance

Are these GTA 6 features actually PS5 exclusive?

Rockstar’s marketing might make you think PS5 players will get access to features that Xbox Series X/S users won’t be able to experience. However, that’s not entirely true. The thing to note here is that Sony has a marketing deal with Rockstar, which explains why PlayStation branding is all over GTA 6 trailers, and why the game is being promoted as playing best on PS5. It’s a way for Sony to associate its brand with one of the biggest game releases in history.

However, the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S versions of GTA 6 are all set to bring the same gameplay experience. The real difference comes in how the game uses the PS5’s DualSense controller. Features such as haptic feedback and adaptive triggers simply aren’t present on Xbox controllers. The game plans to use these features to make Jason and Lucia’s journey feel more immersive. The PS5 Pro should also deliver a better experience compared to the base consoles, as it packs more powerful hardware.

Every GTA 6 PS5 feature explained

We’ve already covered all the GTA 6 PS5 features you need to know about in the table above. Now, let’s take a closer look at each feature and explain how it could enhance your overall gameplay experience on Sony’s console.

1. Tempest 3D audio

Rockstar Games has gone out of its way with GTA 6’s audio design, from its soundtrack featuring the likes of Travis Scott, Keith Richards, and PinkPantheress to environmental sounds that bring Leonida to life. On PS5, players will be able to take advantage of Sony’s Tempest 3D AudioTech for a more immersive sound experience. It can make in-game audio feel more realistic and spatial, making the world feel even more alive.

2. SSD loading

If there’s one thing GTA 5 players have dealt with for years, it’s loading screens. Thankfully, the PS5’s high-speed SSD should make this less of an issue in GTA 6. The console’s storage technology allows game data to load much faster, which reduces the time players spend waiting to get back into the action. PlayStation has described it as “near-instant load times”, which should make moving around Leonida and completing missions feel like a breeze.

3. Adaptive triggers

The DualSense controller’s adaptive triggers are designed to make in-game actions feel different depending on what’s happening on screen. In GTA 6, this could make activities like driving and shooting feel more realistic. You will feel changes in trigger resistance when firing weapons, or different levels of tension during intense encounters. These small details can make the game feel even more engaging.

4. Haptic feedback

PS5’s haptic feedback will be a game-changer in GTA 6. You will feel the impact of explosions, the fumble of a vehicle, and even the sensation of parachuting through the air. Even smaller interactions will produce vibrations and add another layer of immersion as you explore Leonida.

5. Integrated speaker

Another feature that GTA 6 plans to use is the DualSense’s integrated speaker. Combined with haptics, it could make certain moments feel more immediate by letting you hear and feel part of the action through the controller itself. We’ll have to wait for more gameplay details to learn exactly how this plays out.

Is GTA 6 PS5 Pro Enhanced? What we know

Over on the PlayStation Store, GTA 6 has been listed as PS5 Pro Enhanced. This means that the game can make use of the hardware capabilities of Sony’s most powerful console. Unfortunately, the listing doesn’t exactly tell us what these improvements will look like.

We don’t know whether PS5 Pro owners will get higher frame rates or improvements to certain aspects of the game. One of the biggest unanswered questions is whether GTA 6 will offer a dedicated 60 FPS mode on the console. Until Rockstar shares more information about the game’s performance, it’s too early to say how much of an advantage the PS5 Pro will have over the standard console.

Will GTA 6 run at 60 FPS on PS5?

While the PS5 Pro should bring some improvements over the standard PS5, it’s still unclear whether either console will be able to run GTA 6 at 60 FPS. Rockstar Games hasn’t confirmed a 60 FPS mode for the PS5, PS5 Pro, or even Xbox Series X/S.

According to YouTuber Davy Jones, who had the opportunity to visit Rockstar North and chat with the game’s co-director Rob Nelson, GTA 6 is targeting 30 FPS at launch. However, Nelson said he would need to check with his technical team on whether a 60 FPS mode could be made available at launch or later.

What’s interesting to note is that speculation about GTA 6 running at 60 FPS on the PS5 Pro picked up again in August 2026. This was when well-known insider HipHopGamer made claims about the game’s performance on the upgraded console. However, Rockstar hasn’t officially backed up these claims, so it’s better to wait for more details before drawing any conclusions.

How to set up your PS5 for GTA 6 before Nov 19

If you’re planning to jump into GTA 6 the moment it launches, here’s a list of things we recommend doing beforehand to make sure your PS5 is ready for the game:

1. Free up storage space

It’s rumored that GTA 6 could take over 200 GB of storage, based on the reported size of a development build. While Rockstar hasn’t confirmed the exact file size yet, it’s a good idea to clear some space on your PS5 before pre-loads begin on November 12. Even the boxed edition contains a download code rather than a disc, so everyone will need the space. Here’s how to do that:

  1. Open Settings on your PS5.
  2. Select Storage.
  3. Choose Console Storage to see how much space is available.
  4. Delete games or applications you no longer use if you need more room.
  5. Leave some extra space for game updates.

2. Update your PS5 system software

Before GTA 6 launches, make sure your PS5 is running the latest system software. Keeping your console updated can prevent compatibility issues and ensure you have the latest system improvements. Follow these steps to check for updates:

  1. Open Settings on your PS5
  2. Choose System, then go to System Software.
  3. Select System Software Update and Settings.
  4. Hit Update System Software and install any available updates.

Once your PS5 is updated and ready, you can also adjust its display, audio, performance preset, and DualSense options.

See our guide to the PS5 settings to change for the best GTA 6 experience.

GTA 6 limited-edition DualSense controllers

Rockstar Games and Sony have something special in store for GTA fans, with limited-edition DualSense controllers inspired by GTA 6. These are available in two variants, Black and White, and feature designs inspired by Vice City’s neon-lit nightlife, palm trees, and iconic sunsets alongside the official GTA 6 branding. The Black edition is exclusive to PlayStation Direct, while the White edition is also sold through other retailers.

Of course, they still come with all the usual DualSense features, including the likes of haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, and a touchpad. Priced at $84.99, these controllers launch on November 19 and are produced in limited quantities, so be quick to get one before they’re gone.

Once you launch the game, see our guide to the best GTA 6 settings for in-game controls, subtitles, navigation, and accessibility options.

GTA 6 PS5 price and editions

GTA 6 comes in two editions: Standard and Ultimate, each offering a different set of in-game bonuses. If you’re wondering which version to buy, we’ve put together a breakdown of all GTA 6 versions to help you make the right call. However, if you want a quick overview, here’s what you can expect from each version:

Wrapping up

GTA 6 is shaping up to be one of the biggest releases of the year, and PS5 players have a confirmed advantage in how the game uses the DualSense controller. Haptic feedback and adaptive triggers are designed to make the action feel more immersive, while the PS5 Pro listing confirms that the game is enhanced for Sony’s more powerful console.

However, not every feature associated with PS5 is exclusive to it. Both PS5 and Xbox Series X/S use SSD storage, and Rockstar hasn’t confirmed that PlayStation players will receive exclusive story content. We also don’t yet know whether either PS5 model will offer a 60 FPS mode at launch.

With the November 19 release date approaching, more technical details may emerge. Until then, keep your console updated, make room for the installation, and check official announcements for confirmed performance specifications.

FAQs

Will GTA 6 support all DualSense features?

PlayStation has confirmed support for DualSense haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, and the integrated speaker. However, exactly how each feature is used in specific missions and moments hasn’t been detailed yet.

Is GTA 6 coming to PS4?

No. GTA 6 is scheduled to launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar has not announced a PS4 version.

Will GTA 6 look better on PS5 than Xbox?
