title.rendered: John Ternus is still hands-on with Apple’s design teams

content.rendered:
Apple CEO John Ternus has spent multiple days a week in the studio with the company’s industrial-design and human-interface teams, according to TIME’s reporting. Andrew R. Chow interviewed him for TIME in September, after Ternus took over from Tim Cook on September 1.

TIME published the interview on October 15, ahead of its Best Inventions of 2026 issue, which goes on sale October 26. The full video went up on YouTube on October 20, and 9to5Mac’s writeup of it focused on the design comments. The interview also covers the iPhone Duo, memory shortages, and AI.

Ternus pushed the Duo team to keep working while rivals shipped

Richard Dinh, Apple’s VP of product design, recounts a moment when he asked Ternus whether the team should use a surface material similar to competitors’. Ternus replied, “Look, Rich, you’ll know when it’s the right thing.” According to TIME, that answer gave the team the confidence to push further. Ternus also encouraged the team to invest more time and effort even as rivals reached the market first. Tim Cook, now executive chairman, has said separately that he is not meddling with Ternus.

Hardware and software teams built the Duo together

The iPhone Duo folds to about passport size and opens into a tablet-sized screen. TIME names Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8 as its closest rival, and early testers say the crease is barely noticeable. TIME cites those testers without independent tests.

TIME reports that hardware and software teams worked together on the Duo’s display engine and on moving the main controls to the right side of the screen. The hinge has more than 100 small interior parts, and the Duo’s surface is matte and light-deflecting.

Design decisions on the Duo have drawn other reports. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple dropped a shorter Apple Pencil for the Duo before production.

Dinh credits Ternus with the collaboration: “John was really at the center of driving the spirit of collaboration across the company.”

An engineer who filed a foldable patent in 2011

Ternus studied mechanical engineering and joined Apple in 2001 as an engineer. In 2011, he and five other engineers filed a patent for foldable devices. That puts his interest in foldables more than a decade before the Duo.

In the full video, Ternus says he has worked hand in hand with industrial designers since he joined Apple, according to 9to5Mac’s writeup. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman had already reported in October 2025 that Ternus was the leading candidate to succeed Cook, nearly a year before the handoff.

On rival foldables, Ternus told TIME, “The other examples in the world felt kind of cheap and crappy.”

He also said Apple doesn’t have to make every part of a product itself. He said the company tries to “constrain ourselves to the stuff that matters most.”

The Duo’s success is far from guaranteed

TIME calls the Duo’s success “far from guaranteed” and says many buyers may balk at its price.

title.rendered: Perplexity Computer can now run fully locally on Mac

content.rendered:
Perplexity says its Computer agent can now run fully locally on Mac. The model, the agent harness, and task execution all run on the device, so personal files and apps can be handled without sending that data to the cloud. The feature is called Local Computer on Mac, and it is available now to Pro, Max, and Enterprise subscribers.

Perplexity’s example is a portfolio analysis that combines private holdings with downloaded market data. It is the kind of task people may not want to send to a cloud service. Local Computer builds on Personal Computer for Mac, which launched in May and gave Computer access to local files and native Mac apps.

Planning, reasoning, and files stay on the Mac

In fully local mode, planning, reasoning, and file processing run on the device. The model is either Qwen 3.6 or PPLX Pro, which Perplexity describes as a post-trained version of Qwen. Code and tool execution run in isolated sandbox environments with controlled access to files and connected apps. Computer works across local files and supported apps, including Notes, Messages, Mail, and Numbers.

Web and connected-app tasks still use the cloud

Tasks that need current information, browser use, or cloud-connected apps need the user’s approval before they go to the cloud. The local orchestrator can also call one of more than 15 frontier models for harder reasoning. Perplexity doesn’t say how often that happens in local mode, so “fully local” describes the on-device default. It is not a promise that no cloud model is involved.

Perplexity also doesn’t say how many credits a local run uses. Users choose where each task runs and how to spend their credits.

Perplexity recommends 36GB of memory

Perplexity says the feature works on “supported Apple silicon Macs” but doesn’t name the models. It gives no minimum memory or macOS version. It does recommend 36GB or more for running Computer locally. Perplexity points to the new Mac mini as an example of a supported machine. The M6 Mac mini tops out at 32GB of unified memory, which falls short of that recommendation. Buyers who want local mode should check the memory configuration before they buy.

Big local models need a lot of memory

Local AI depends on memory. Meta says two M5 Ultra Mac Studios can host its 816-billion-parameter Muse Spark Open model. Moonshot’s Kimi K3 open weights take up roughly 1.56TB, which puts them out of reach for most MacBooks. Perplexity hasn’t said how large its local models are, so the 36GB figure is the best guide for now.

Who gets it and how to set it up

content.rendered:

Looking for Shigaku codes? Well, gamer, you’re at the right place! Luckily, we’ve got you covered with a complete list of all Shigaku codes that can be redeemed for Rerolls and Cash. So, make sure to grab these freebies as soon as possible!

All working Shigaku codes

Expired Shigaku codes

How to redeem Shigaku codes in Roblox

Knowing the active codes isn’t enough, gamers! You also need to know how to redeem them and claim your free rewards. Thankfully, the process only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Shigaku codes:

  1. Fire up Shigaku on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on the Menu button and then open Settings.
  4. Find the Codes box.
  5. Paste a working code and hit Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Why aren’t my Shigaku codes working?

If your Shigaku codes aren’t working, double-check that you’ve entered them exactly as listed above. Keep in mind that these codes are case-sensitive, so make sure there are no extra spaces before or after them. You can simply copy and paste the codes directly from our list. If a code still doesn’t work, it might’ve expired, or you may have already redeemed its rewards.

How to get more Shigaku codes

The developers don’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new Shigaku codes. Most codes are released to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Discord server: Visit the Shigaku Discord server to find announcements and newly released codes.

  • Bookmark this page: We’ll update this guide whenever new Shigaku codes become available, so you can easily find the latest rewards in one place.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Kaiju Alpha codes, Smash a Piggy codes, Turbo Soccer codes and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

What rewards can you get from Shigaku codes?

Shigaku codes are used to obtain free Rerolls, which allow you to change your character’s appearance, fighting abilities, surname and more. Some codes can also provide Cash.

Do Shigaku codes expire?

Shigaku codes expire after a certain date. Codes are released to celebrate major milestones or updates, so their availability is limited.

What are the best fighting styles in Shigaku?

Some of the best fighting styles in Shigaku are Karate and boxing. These styles are all about being aggressive and applying forward pressure on your enemies.

title.rendered: How to unlock and find Finger Guns in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Finger Guns are back in Fortnite, thanks to their surprise addition in the October 15 update, the final major content drop for the Fortnite Override season. This dual-wielded weapon originally debuted in the game on April Fools’ Day 2026 to a rather positively stirring reception, making their comeback a notable highlight.

In itself, Finger Guns are not really ‘guns’ that you can equip. Upon selecting the weapon, the game just makes your character gesture his fingers in roughly the form of a gun that fires bullets with a humorous “Pew! Pew!” sound, as the same thing also appears on the screen like comic book text.

In this guide, you can learn how to unlock and then find Finger Guns in Fortnite. Additionally, you can also check out other items in the loot hack pool below.

How to unlock Finger Guns in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Override tab.
  2. Under Loot Hack, highlight the Finger Guns item.
  3. Lastly, press and hold the Unlock/Upgrade button to add Finger Guns to your loot pool.

How to find Finger Guns in Fortnite

Once you have unlocked the Finger Guns loot item, you can find it by opening chests. To boost your chances of finding it via this method, it is recommended to use any of the Loot Hacker sprites available in the game.

In addition, as you gather enough Sprite Dust through sprite extractions or Fortnite Lobby Hacks, make sure to keep upgrading Finger Guns from the aforementioned Loot Hack tab. Doing so will further increase the likelihood of getting this weapon from chests, with almost every successive upgrade—two of these levels unlock higher rarity for Finger Guns instead of a better spawn rate.

Given below is how the Finger Guns spawn rate changes at each of its five upgrade levels.

  • Upgrade 1: 5% drop rate when opening a chest
  • Upgrade 2: Epic rarity as the highest possible tier
  • Upgrade 3: 8% drop rate when opening a chest
  • Upgrade 4: 10% drop rate when opening a chest
  • Upgrade 5: Legendary rarity as the highest possible tier

Other Loot Hacks in Fortnite Override right now

Similar to how Finger Guns is a part of the new lineup of loot hacks in Fortnite Override, there are other items as well on the same list. These range from sniper rifles to health consumables and are listed below.

1. All sprite variants

2. Gatekeeper Shotgun

3. Hunting Rifle

4. Thorne’s Vampiric Blade

5. Slap Splash

Final thoughts

While they may seem hilarious on the surface, Finger Guns are no joke when it comes to dealing damage and a reasonable rate of fire. Hence, it would be a good decision if this item is one of the first things that you unlock and max out using Sprite Dust. It’s also worth remembering that even if you have already unlocked or upgraded an item, you can always undo that decision and re-allocate the spent Sprite Dust per your whim.

Finger Guns, in the current Loot Hack pool of Fortnite, are perhaps only second to the Thorne’s Vampiric Blade, which is a highly powerful melee weapon. So, according to your playstyle, you should upgrade one or the other as a priority.

It will be interesting to see which of these two emerges as the more popular item in the Fortnite community, as more players get accustomed to them. In any case, once you have both items maxed out, you will more or less be well-prepared for both close-range and medium-range face-offs—that’s a given.

Level up your gaming setup:

  • Logitech G Astro A10 Wired Gaming Headset
  • SteelSeries Aeon Pro Wireless Controller
  • CyberPowerPC Gaming PC (GeForce RTX 5060)
  • Razer Naga V3 Pro Gaming Mouse
  • Redragon Mechanical Gaming Keyboard
  • Ergonomic Gaming Chair (Adjustable Lumbar Support)

title.rendered: All Droid Fusion recipes in Fortnite Star Wars Droid Tycoon

content.rendered:
Since its release in May, as part of a major collab between Fortnite and Star Wars, the Star Wars Droid Tycoon map has received significantly positive reception from fans and continues to attract a sizable audience compared to other third-party Fortnite maps. Then, in August, its developer FOAD rolled out a new update that threw droid fusion into the mix, which essentially introduced new droids for players to add to their collection.

Since then, players have been trying different combos and learning about which ‘recipe’ works for generating which kind of droid. While it may seem like a mostly hit-and-trial process, there are actually fixed recipes out in the community that provide a specific droid when put into action. All such fusion recipes are shared later in this article.

How Droid Fusion works in Star Wars Droid Tycoon

The fusion feature in Star Wars Droid Tycoon involves combining three different droids to either obtain a variant of a higher rarity or a new droid itself. It goes without saying that the droids used to construct a new one will be permanently lost.

This gameplay mechanic is only accessible to players who have reached Rebirth 3 on the progression chart, which is quite convenient to reach. This Rebirth level requires a player to have 975K credits along with base A-LT, base B-U4D, and gold R9 droids. Eligible players can take part in droid fusion by visiting the Fusion Lab, which is sandwiched between the landing zone of your base and the workshop location.

All Droid Fusion recipes in Star Wars Droid Tycoon

The list below encompasses all the droids you can create via droid fusion in Star Wars Droid Tycoon. From droids of the Rare tier to those of the Mythic tier, you will find the respective recipe to construct each of them.

Wrapping up

In its heyday, Star Wars Droid Tycoon used to pull tens of thousands of concurrent Fortnite players daily. While that has now dropped to around 20K peak concurrent players in a day, the game is still on the higher side on the list of Fortnite UEFN maps that get the most user engagement.

In fact, the game’s popularity has enabled FOAD to ship regular updates so far, including one from last month that optimized the experience for mobile users. This should naturally rope in more players and give some boost to the footfall that this Fortnite map gets. However, only time will tell if the newly gained audience stays over the long term.

title.rendered: What is Apple Watch for Your Kids and how does it work?

content.rendered:
Apple Watch for Your Kids, formerly known as Family Setup, lets a parent set up a cellular Apple Watch for a child or older family member who doesn’t have an iPhone. The parent manages the watch from their own iPhone. Here’s what it does, what you need now, and how to set it up.

What is Apple Watch For Your Kids?

With Apple Watch for Kids, a parent or guardian can set up Apple Watch with cellular for kids or older people who do not have their own iPhones. The parent can use their iPhone to manage the kids’ Apple Watch.

Once set up, kids can use the Apple Watch freely without needing an iPhone. They can go to school, sports practice, a picnic, and anywhere without any concern, and the parent can know their whereabouts.

What can kids do with Apple Watch For Your Kids?

  • Make and receive FaceTime audio calls and standard phone calls.
  • Send and receive messages and emails.
  • Connect Apple Watch to AirPods or any Bluetooth earphones & speaker and use Apple Music.
  • Use Apple Cash Family (US only): This lets parents load money to kids’ Apple Watch, which they can utilize wherever Apple Pay is accepted.
  • Have kid-oriented personalized Activity goals/Activity rings.
  • Use custom Memoji right from the Apple Watch using its Memoji app.
  • Use safety and everyday features without needing an iPhone, like Emergency SOS, Maps, Siri, Alarms, and the App Store.

What family members can do with their Apple Watch?

Receive emergency SOS notifications

If the parents or guardians are set as emergency contacts (which they should be), they’ll be notified in emergencies. Kids can look at their Medical ID for relevant information. Plus, the guardian can also view the health and activity of their family members using the iPhone’s Health app.

Set Schooltime Schedule

During Schooltime, the kid’s Apple Watch shows a yellow circle on the watch face. This helps the teachers in the classroom (or parent tutoring at home) easily recognize the apps whose access is restricted, plus Do Not Disturb can be enabled on the kid’s Apple Watch.

Apple Cash Family

This lets the parents load money to the kid’s watch via Apple Pay and choose to receive notifications when they spend it. The parent can even see the kid’s purchases in the Wallet app on the iPhone. This is a fine example of training the young generation for the coming cashless future!

Other Features

  • Parents can allow certain contacts, and kids will be able to communicate only with these approved persons.
  • Set content restrictions and Ask to Buy: This lets the parents manage which category of apps are available for download on the kid’s Apple Watch. Ask to Buy sends the parent an approval notification when the kid tries to purchase an app or make an in-app purchase.
  • Share the kid’s location through Find My, so you can see where they are on your iPhone. Parents can also get location notifications, such as when the kid reaches school or basketball practice.

How to set up an Apple Watch for a family member

Before You Begin:

  • Make sure the iPhone runs iOS 27, and the watch supports watchOS 27. The model list is in the compatibility section below.
  • Turn ON Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on the iPhone.
  • Erase the Apple Watch if it isn’t new.
  • Make sure you have an Apple Account for yourself (the parent or guardian). The child gets their own phone number and Apple Account with the watch.
  • Family Sharing: Setup creates a group if you don’t have one. The child must be in your Family Sharing group with a Child Account.
  1. Have your child put on the Apple Watch and press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears.
  2. Bring the watch near the iPhone. Wait for a moment, and you should see “Use your iPhone to set up this Apple Watch” on the iPhone screen. Tap on Continue. After this, tap on Set Up for a Family Member → Continue. If you don’t see this, open the Watch app on iPhone, go to My Watch → All Watches, and tap Add Watch.
  3. Point the iPhone over the animation on the Apple Watch screen. You will see a message that says the Apple Watch is successfully paired.
  4. Agree to the terms and conditions (if you do), select text size, and set a passcode for the Apple Watch.
  5. Select a family member from the screen or tap on Add New Family Member. Now, enter the kid’s (or the family member’s) Apple Account and password, then proceed. It is a good idea to tap on Turn on Ask to Buy. (more about it above)
  6. If your carrier supports Apple Watch for Your Kids, you can add the watch to your plan during this step. If it doesn’t, or you want a different carrier, tap Not Now and contact a supported carrier to set up the plan. Then set up Wi-Fi and turn on other options like location, Siri, Apple Cash Family, Health data, etc. You can also set up Schooltime and shared contacts. Once you are done, tap on OK. Now, the kid can start using the Apple Watch.

Family Setup compatible Apple Watch and iPhone

Family Setup is available on cellular models of Apple Watch Series 4 and later running watchOS 7. You can pair the watch with iPhone 6s and later running iOS 14.

Note: Apple says that ‘a cellular plan isn’t required to set up an Apple Watch for a family member, but is necessary for some features.’

Compatible Apple Watch and iPhone models

Apple recommends the Apple Watch SE 3 with GPS + Cellular. The watch has to be a cellular model that runs watchOS 27: Series 9 or later, SE 3, or Ultra 2 or later. Older models, including Series 8 and SE (2nd generation), can’t run watchOS 27, so check the model before you reuse an old watch.

The iPhone needs iOS 27 for watchOS 27. Apple’s requirement is an iPhone 11 or later, or an iPhone SE (2nd generation) or later.

Note: You don’t need a cellular plan to finish setup. The watch does need an active plan to connect to a cellular network, though, and some features depend on it.

Regions and carriers that support Family Setup

At launch, 18 carriers in 12 countries and regions support Family Setup. This is a carrier support-oriented feature (separate phone number, data plan, etc.) Thus, in the coming months, it will expand to other regions and carriers as well. For more information, like availability and pricing, contact your carrier.

Views on Family Setup

What are your thoughts on Apple Watch Family Setup? Is this something you are excited about? Are you planning to use it in your family? Please let us know in the comments down below.

In my opinion, this is a great feature. Now, you can give the kid an affordable Apple Watch SE or your old Series 5, and they get the power to stay safely connected to people that matter.

One thing that I feel strange is that Apple discontinued Series 4 and 5 but kept Series 3. And unfortunately, Family Setup requires Series 4 and above. So, that’s a bummer!

Now, instead of giving a smartphone, it is convenient to have a powerful tiny computer on the child’s wrist (that they won’t misplace) when at baseball practice or a friend’s house. Likewise, it lets you keep track of older people more conveniently.

Overall, I think it’s a smart move to get Apple Watch to more people in an affordable way!

title.rendered: WhatsApp is building an in-app browser for links in iPhone chats

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is developing an in-app browser for iPhone that would open any link shared in a chat inside the app, WABetaInfo reported on October 19. The site found the feature in WhatsApp beta for iOS 26.41.10.72 on TestFlight. It is not yet available to beta testers, and WhatsApp has not announced it.

WABetaInfo says WhatsApp will make the browser available to some beta testers in a future update. No public release date has been given.

Links would open without leaving the conversation

Tapping a link in a chat would load the page inside the conversation screen instead of switching to Safari or another browser. According to WABetaInfo, the browser runs in a session separate from the chat. The three-dot menu would still open the page in your default browser.

WABetaInfo describes this as an AI expansion of an earlier feature that covered only certain business links. That version appeared in iOS beta 25.14.10.72 in May 2025, and WABetaInfo says it reached the Android beta first. Sites had to use HTTPS and meet other technical requirements, and WhatsApp applied its own business criteria, so some businesses were left out. The October 19 report does not say whether that version has since reached everyone.

A setting would turn it on and clear its data

Users would turn the browser on from an “In-app browser” option in WhatsApp’s settings. A bottom sheet would explain the feature the first time it is enabled. A Browser settings section would let people clear cookies and cache from sites they opened in WhatsApp, and they could restore the default browser at any time.

The privacy claims come from WABetaInfo

WABetaInfo says WhatsApp cannot see the links shared in a conversation, and that neither WhatsApp nor Apple can see which links users open. It also says browsing data is stored on the device, as it is in Safari. WhatsApp has not confirmed any of it.

It follows a run of WhatsApp changes to chats and links

WhatsApp has been changing the iPhone chat screen this month. A Liquid Glass menu in the chat header began rolling out on October 9, and its shortcuts include media, links, and docs. On October 14, WhatsApp launched guest calling, where a host shares a call link and people without an account join from a computer browser.

WhatsApp has set no timeline for the browser

The report covers WhatsApp for iOS and does not mention Android. The gap between a build and a rollout can be short. The Liquid Glass progress bar for the video player was in development in an August beta and not available to testers, and WABetaInfo reported it rolling out on October 6, less than two months later. WhatsApp has given no schedule for the browser.

The report does not describe any warning for suspicious links. WhatsApp’s scam tools so far, such as the alerts it has tested when you message someone who is not in your contacts, apply to contacts and groups. If the browser opens every link in a chat, the first thing to check when it ships is whether it warns you about risky pages.

title.rendered: Apple reportedly plans a larger HomeView with a 9-inch screen on a robotic arm

content.rendered:
Apple is planning a higher-end HomeView with a 9-inch screen that swivels a full 360 degrees on a robotic arm, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. He wrote in his October 18 Power On newsletter that he expects the device to launch in 2027 or 2028. Apple has not announced it, and no name or price has been reported.

The current HomeView is the one Apple announced on October 13. It has a 7-inch screen on a domed speaker base, and a hinge tilts the display up or down. It costs $299 and ships November 13.

The reported model adds a bigger screen and an arm that turns

The model Gurman describes would put a 9-inch display on a robotic arm that can turn it through a full circle. The current HomeView’s screen only tilts.

iClarified and The Apple Post, both summarizing the newsletter, add two details. The device carries the internal codename J595, and it would use voice recognition to work out who is speaking and turn the screen toward that person.

Both describe the device as an addition to the lineup that sits above the $299 model. The Apple Post compares the turning screen to Center Stage, which the current HomeView uses in FaceTime calls to keep participants framed. The reports do not mention the new model’s chip or camera.

Gurman expects 2027 or 2028 and has only floated names

The launch window covers two years. Gurman suggested the names HomeView Max, HomeView Ultra, and HomeView 360, and the names are speculative. Apple has not used any of the three.

No price has been reported. iClarified’s summary says Gurman suspects Apple kept the current HomeView at $299 by building units early, before this year’s memory shortage raised component costs. A bigger screen, a motor, and a place above the $299 model point to a higher price.

Pre-orders for the 7-inch model are open now, and Apple’s October 13 announcement does not mention a larger one.

Bloomberg has tracked a robotic-arm device since 2024

Gurman reported in August 2024 that Apple was developing a tabletop device that uses a thin robotic arm to move a large screen. Actuators would tilt the display up and down and spin it 360 degrees. It was described as a smart home command center, a video-calling machine, and a remote-controlled home security tool.

In August 2025, Bloomberg reported that the tabletop robot was targeted for 2027. That report described a display of about 7 inches on a motorized arm that could extend about six inches from its base. It placed a stationary smart home hub ahead of the robot, in 2026, and that hub arrived this month as HomeView.

Set against those reports, the new one raises the screen from about 7 inches to 9 and adds 2028 as a possible launch year.

The first hub slipped more than a year, so dates can move

HomeView was originally meant to launch in March 2025, alongside Siri’s AI overhaul. Gurman reported that Siri’s problems pushed the hub to 2026. Apple announced it on October 13 with Siri AI still in beta. The larger model is built around voice recognition, so its date could depend on Siri as well.

Early size reports have moved before

Bloomberg’s September 30 report on the display that became HomeView put its screen at 6 inches. Apple announced a 7-inch display on October 13. A size reported this far ahead of a launch is a plan that can still change, and Apple has not confirmed the 9-inch figure or anything else in the report.

title.rendered: Gurman says Apple made a “major mistake” with iPhone Duo pre-orders

content.rendered:
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple made a "major mistake" by opening iPhone Duo pre-orders on Friday, October 16, despite knowing manufacturing problems would leave supply severely constrained. He made the claim in his Power On newsletter on October 18.

Pre-orders for Apple’s first foldable iPhone, which starts at $1,999, opened at 5 a.m. Pacific. Within 30 minutes, Apple’s U.S. online store showed January 25 delivery for every configuration. Apple has not publicly addressed Gurman’s claim. It has said pre-order demand was "nothing short of extraordinary."

Gurman says Apple put an early launch ahead of inventory

Gurman writes that Apple could have waited for more stock before taking orders. He says it prioritized having the phone out early in its fiscal first quarter, which covers the holiday period, over meeting demand. He expects the shortage to disappoint early adopters.

The claim about Apple’s reasons is Gurman’s reading. Apple has not said how many phones it had when pre-orders opened or whether it expected demand to outrun supply.

The risk was public beforehand. Bloomberg had reported that Apple expected limited availability at launch and had worried that manufacturing constraints could push some sales into November. Nikkei Asia reported in early September that production was only a few hundred units a day in late August. With those warnings out for weeks, delivery dates slipping within minutes was predictable.

Pre-orders opened in 70-plus countries at once

According to Gurman, Apple originally planned to launch the iPhone Duo only in the U.S. and China, with other countries following later. It opened pre-orders in more than 70 countries and regions instead, which spreads the available stock across far more markets.

Apple’s September announcement already listed those markets for the October 23 launch, with 28 more countries and regions on October 30. The wide rollout was public before pre-orders began.

Delivery dates passed Christmas within half an hour

Buyers who ordered at about 5 a.m. Pacific were promised delivery on October 23, launch day. By 5:30 a.m., Apple’s U.S. store listed January 25 for Star White and Night Sky in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB. 9to5Mac reported that estimates in some countries, including Brazil, moved into early February.

MacRumors notes that Apple tends to underpromise, so some customers may receive their phones a little before the listed date. Apple’s online store can no longer deliver before Christmas.

Anyone who needs a foldable before then has one already on sale: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold starts at $1,899 for 256GB.

Walk-in stock on October 23 looks unlikely

MacRumors reported on October 17 that Apple Store employees were told there will likely be no iPhone Duo stock for walk-in customers on launch day. Staff were told to discourage people without pre-orders from coming in. MacRumors says it is unclear how firm the guidance is or whether it applies to every store. Apple has not said publicly whether any stores will have walk-in stock.

Apple briefly offered store pickup during pre-orders, then turned it off. Its online store now says to check back on Saturday, October 24, for pickup availability. That message does not promise stock on that day.

Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile took pre-orders too, and Best Buy sells the phone, so their delivery dates are separate from Apple’s online store. For pickup on October 24, check Apple’s website or the Apple Store app.

title.rendered: HomePod mini 2 vs Echo Studio: Which speaker should you buy?

content.rendered:
Most of this decision comes down to two things: which phone you use, and how much speaker you want. The HomePod mini 2 is the small option. It costs $149, weighs 335 g, and sits on a shelf without taking over. The Echo Studio (2025) is the big one. It costs $219.99, weighs 1.63 kg, and doubles as a smart home hub with Zigbee, Thread, and Matter built in.

If you’re on an iPhone and want something small, the HomePod mini 2 is the one I’d look at first. If you’re on Android, or you want bigger sound and a hub that does more, the Echo Studio is the better fit.

HomePod mini 2 vs Echo Studio at a glance

Start with your phone: iPhone vs Android

The HomePod mini 2 needs an iPhone or iPad for setup, and Apple lists a compatible device as a system requirement. The Echo Studio, on the other hand, works with both Android and iPhone, making it a more flexible choice if your household uses different phone platforms. If you’re on Android and don’t have access to an iPhone or iPad, the HomePod mini 2 isn’t the right option for you.

But compatibility goes beyond initial setup. With the HomePod mini 2, you’ll get the best experience if you’re already invested in Apple’s ecosystem, especially if you use Apple Music, the Home app, and other Apple devices. You can use Siri to control supported smart home accessories, manage music playback, and access other Apple services.

The Echo Studio is a better fit for households that prefer Alexa, use Android phones, or rely on Alexa-compatible smart home devices. You can manage Alexa settings and connected devices through the Alexa app, without needing to own an iPhone.

My take: If you already use an iPhone and other Apple devices, the HomePod mini 2 makes more sense. But if you want a smart speaker that fits into an Android household just as easily, the Echo Studio is the more practical choice. Your existing phone and smart home setup should be the first things you consider before deciding between these two speakers.

Size and sound

The Echo Studio is nearly five times heavier than the HomePod mini 2. Amazon’s 2025 model is about 40% smaller than the original Echo Studio, but it’s still a big speaker that needs a shelf of its own.

Reviews split on bass. Tom’s Guide says the Echo Studio makes a lot of bass for its size. Expert Reviews says the bass isn’t as strong as the original Echo Studio’s, but it calls the speaker better than anything else in Amazon’s range for filling a room, and it praises the wide sound with Dolby Atmos music from Amazon Music.

Reviews of the HomePod mini 2 were hard to find at the time of writing, and Apple doesn’t publish driver size or power. Wait for reviews before you judge its sound against the Echo.

Which is the better smart home hub?

The Echo Studio connects Zigbee devices without a separate bridge, and it handles Thread and Matter too. It also has presence detection built in.

The HomePod mini 2 covers Thread networking for HomeKit and Matter accessories, and it adds temperature and humidity sensors. Apple’s spec page doesn’t list Zigbee, so Zigbee devices need another hub.

The HomePod mini 2’s Sound Recognition listens for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Apple warns that detection may not be reliable, so keep your real alarms in place.

Alexa+ vs Siri AI: Which assistant is ready now?

Alexa+ is live on the Echo Studio today. Amazon says it’s included at no extra cost with Prime. Without Prime, full access costs $19.99 a month, and a limited text chat is free on Alexa.com and in the Alexa app.

Siri AI is still coming to the HomePod mini 2. Apple says it arrives as a free software update, but it hasn’t given a date. The homeowner needs an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad with Siri AI turned on, and it isn’t available in the EU on iOS or iPadOS at first. Don’t buy the HomePod mini 2 for Siri AI alone.

Price: is the Echo Studio worth $70 more?

The Echo Studio costs about $70 more than the HomePod mini 2. If sound and size matter more than price, Apple’s closer match is the full-size HomePod, which went from $299 to $349 in June 2026.

Which one should you buy?

  • HomePod mini 2: iPhone and iPad owners who want a small speaker, Thread support, and humidity sensing for $149. Skip it if you run Zigbee devices or use Android.
  • Echo Studio (2025): Android owners, Zigbee smart homes, and anyone who wants Dolby Atmos and presence detection. Make sure the listing says 2025, since the original 2019 Echo Studio is a bigger, cylindrical speaker.

Start with your phone, then think about how much room you have. That usually settles it.

title.rendered: How to manage downloads in Safari on iPhone or iPad

content.rendered:
Safari, Apple’s native browser, offers a wide range of features. Like other browsers, it also lets you download files (PDFs, images, and others) from the web with ease. While downloading with Safari is typically easy, many still don’t know how to manage these Safari downloads on iPhone and iPad.

But your daunting thought of how to manage Safari downloads on iPhone and iPad stops here. I’ll discuss everything you should know about downloading files on Safari in this piece. Let’s begin!

Understanding Safari’s download manager

Apple added the download manager in Safari with the release of iOS 13. Thanks to it, you can easily download files from the web and manage them directly from within the Safari browser on your iPhone and iPad.

Here are some key features of Safari’s download manager:

  • Download tracking
  • Download list
  • Pause, resume, or cancel downloads
  • File management
  • Automatic deletion of the download list
  • Compatibility with cloud services like iCloud Drive and Dropbox

Where are Safari downloads stored on an iPhone or iPad?

Your download items on Safari are stored in either iCloud Drive or on your iPhone’s local storage. However, you can choose the preferred location to store them through the Settings app. I’ll cover the steps to do that in a subsequent section of the piece.

Why should you manage downloads in Safari?

Here are some reasons why you should manage your downloads in Safari on your iPhone or iPad:

  • Avoid clutter: If you download a lot of files in Safari, the folder where you save all your downloads can be the most cluttered location in the Files app. But if you regularly manage your downloads by choosing different download locations for some file types, you can better organize your downloads and make them easy to find.
  • Save storage space: Downloads often accumulate a lot of storage space on your devices, and a lot of the time they are those you no longer need. Hence, it’s important to manage them. That way, you can get rid of unnecessary files and free up some storage.
  • Maintain privacy: If you share your iPhone or iPad with someone, managing your downloads is a great way to keep the personal files you’ve downloaded online properly saved or deleted from prying eyes. With the help of features like auto-deletion, you can ensure no one knows the files you’ve downloaded on your device over time.
  • Keep your device secure: You might unintentionally download harmful files online, but by regularly keeping a tab on your downloads, you can easily notice such files and quickly remove them to protect your device from threats.

How to manage Safari download items on iPhone or iPad

Now that you’re familiar with the Safari download manager, let’s see how you can use it to manage your downloads effectively.

Access and view downloads in Safari

You can access and view your downloaded files in both Safari and the Files app. Here’s what the process looks like on each of them.

On Safari:

  1. Tap the Downloads button next to the search field.
  2. Tap Downloads to see your downloaded files.
  3. Tap the downloaded file to open it. Or tap the search icon next to it to open its location in the Files app.

Note: This works if you’ve just downloaded a file via Safari and the download list has not been cleared.

In the Files app:

  1. Launch the Files app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Select Browse, tap iCloud Drive, then open the Downloads folder. If you changed the download location, open that folder instead.

Pause, resume, and cancel downloads in Safari

You can also pause, resume, and cancel downloads in Safari. Here’s how:

  1. In Safari, tap the arrow inscribed in a circle in the left corner of the address bar and select Downloads.
  2. Tap the X icon on your ongoing download to pause it.
  3. To resume the download, tap the curved arrow on the download.
  4. While there’s no dedicated button to cancel a download, if you want to do it anyway, swipe left on an ongoing download and select Delete.

Change the download location in Safari on an iPhone or iPad

Safari lets you store your downloads in iCloud or local storage by default. But you can choose any other location, too. Here’s how:

  1. Head to the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Navigate to Apps, then tap it and select Safari from the app list.
  3. Tap Downloads under General.
  4. On the resulting page, choose where you wan to save your downloads from the available options: iCloud Drive, On My iPhone/iPad, or Other.

Note: Choosing iCloud Drive means your downloads will sync across all devices connected to iCloud.

Delete Safari downloads on an iPhone

You can delete Safari downloads on your iPhone and iPad by going to the location it’s saved in the Files app and deleting the file there. Here are the steps to do that:

  1. Open the Files app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Go to the location where your Safari downloads are saved.
  3. Tap the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.
  4. Next, tap Select, then select the downloaded files you want to delete and tap the trash icon at the bottom.

If you want to delete download items in Safari, you can do that, too.

Delete an individual download:

  1. Go to Downloads in Safari as described earlier.
  2. Swipe left on the downloaded file you want to delete.
  3. Finally, tap the Delete button.

Delete all downloads:

  1. Go to the Downloads page on Safari.
  2. Tap Clear in the top-right corner of the Downloads page.

Auto-delete downloads on an iPhone or iPad

Safari has an auto-delete feature that clears downloaded items after a while. Here’s how to enable it:

  1. Launch the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Scroll down and select Apps.
  3. Select Safari, then tap Downloads under General.
  4. On the resulting page, tap Remove Download List Items.
  5. Here, you’ll be able to choose to remove Safari downloads After One day, Upon Successful Download, or manually. Select either of the first two options to automatically delete your Safari download list items.

Note: This feature only deletes the downloaded items from your Safari downloads manager and not the actual files on your iPhone or iPad.

How to troubleshoot an issue with your Safari downloads on an iPhone and iPad

It’s possible that your Safari downloads are getting stuck or you’re having issues with downloading files via the Safari app on your iPhone or iPad. Here are some ways to fix such issues:

  • Ensure you have a stable internet connection.
  • Restart Safari.
  • Clear Safari cache: This can help fix download issues in the Safari browser. Find more details on how you can clear Safari cache on iPhone and iPad.
  • Ensure you have enough storage space on your iPhone or iPad.
  • Change the download location.
  • Update iOS (and the Safari app) on your iPhone or iPad.

Signing off…

Having discussed how you can manage Safari downloads on iPhone and iPad, I believe you can now easily organize, locate, and delete your Safari downloads.

Also, the troubleshooting tips discussed will be helpful in case you face issues with downloading files on Safari. Let us know if you have any other questions in the comments section.

FAQs

Can I transfer downloads from an iPhone to an iPad?

You can send your downloads from an iPhone to an iPad using AirDrop. However, if you choose to save your downloads on your iCloud Drive, it’ll sync across all devices connected to your iCloud, including your iPad, if it’s connected to iCloud.

Does Safari on iPhone download files in the background?

Yes, Safari on iPhone downloads files in the background.

Do Safari downloads go to iCloud?

Yes, your Safari downloads can go to iCloud, but you have to choose iCloud Drive as your download location for that.

  • How to use Safari iCloud tabs on iPhone, iPad and Mac

aioseo_meta_data.description: Learn how to find, manage, pause, and delete Safari downloads on your iPhone or iPad, change download locations, and troubleshoot common issues.

blockGraphs.question: Can I transfer downloads from an iPhone to an iPad?
blockGraphs.answer: You can send your downloads from an iPhone to an iPad using AirDrop. However, if you choose to save your downloads on your iCloud Drive, it'll sync across all devices connected to your iCloud, including your iPad, if it's connected to iCloud.

blockGraphs.question: Does Safari on iPhone download files in the background?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes, Safari on iPhone downloads files in the background.

blockGraphs.question: Do Safari downloads go to iCloud?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes, your Safari downloads can go to iCloud, but you have to choose iCloud Drive as your download location for that.

keyPoints.title: Safari’s Download Manager Features
keyPoints.explanation: Introduced with iOS 13, Safari's download manager allows users to track, pause, resume, cancel, and manage downloaded files seamlessly within the browser.

keyPoints.title: Where Safari Downloads Are Stored
keyPoints.explanation: Downloads from Safari are stored either in iCloud Drive or locally on your device, with the preferred location adjustable through the Settings app.

keyPoints.title: Reasons to Manage Downloads
keyPoints.explanation: Managing downloads helps avoid clutter, save storage space, maintain privacy, and protect your device from harmful files.

keyPoints.title: Managing Downloads on iPhone and iPad
keyPoints.explanation: You can access downloads directly in Safari via the downloads list or through the Files app, where you can view, pause, resume, delete, and change download locations.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting Safari Download Issues
keyPoints.explanation: If downloads are stuck or failing, ensure a stable internet, clear cache, check storage, update iOS, or change download settings to resolve problems.

title.rendered: I bought an iPhone unlocked vs. through a carrier: Here’s which option is actually better

content.rendered:
When buying a new iPhone, I made the same mistake most people make: I looked at the deal’s price. Apple shows the iPhone at its full retail price, while the carrier deals offer something like “$0/month” or “Get up to $1,200 off.”

At first glance, purchasing from a carrier may seem like a no-brainer. But once you start looking at trade-in requirements, monthly bill credits, financing terms, and what happens if you want to switch carriers, the comparison becomes much more interesting.

Here’s which one you should buy, an unlocked or a carrier-locked iPhone, before chasing the biggest discount.

What does “Unlocked” vs. “Carrier” iPhone mean?

Before comparing prices, I think it is worth clearing up one confusing part of the iPhone buying process: “unlocked” and “carrier” don’t always describe where you bought the phone. They depend on how it was financed.

An iPhone purchased directly from Apple is generally unlocked. If you pay in full or finance it through Apple Card Monthly Installments, you receive an unlocked model that can be activated with a compatible carrier. Even if you choose a carrier when purchasing, you can change carriers later and use a different carrier’s SIM or eSIM.

However, if you finance the iPhone through AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon’s installment programs, whether at Apple or on the carrier’s website, the phone remains locked to that carrier until it is paid in full. Apple applied this rule to T-Mobile and Verizon financing in July 2026; before that, only Financed iPhones bought from Apple were locked.

There’s another option that deserves its own category: Apple Upgrade, Apple’s new leasing program run by Klarna, which replaced the iPhone Upgrade Program in July 2026. An iPhone leased through Apple Upgrade is always unlocked, even if you choose a carrier when enrolling. Just remember it’s a lease: you don’t own the iPhone unless you pay off the remaining balance at the end of the term.

I compared the real cost, not just the advertised price

I don’t care whether an advertisement says an iPhone is “$0/month” until I know what I have to do to get that $0 price.

Carrier promotions can be extremely generous, offering hundreds of dollars in credits. For the iPhone 18 Pro, AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon are advertising up to $1,200 off, depending on the deal, trade-in, and eligibility. Their financing can also spread the cost over 24 or 36 months at 0% APR.

That can be a fantastic deal. But the headline price isn’t the number you should use to compare an unlocked iPhone with a carrier iPhone.

The actual iPhone cost calculation

I think about it like this:

Total cost = phone payments + required plan costs + fees − trade-in value − promotional credits

For example, you can:

Buy unlocked

  • Pay the full price of the iPhone.
  • Keep your existing phone plan.
  • Trade in your old phone if you want.
  • Switch carriers whenever you need.

Or you can:

Buy through a carrier

  • Finance the iPhone.
  • Trade in your old phone.
  • Receive monthly bill credits.
  • Keep an eligible carrier plan for the required period.

The second option might look dramatically cheaper. But if you wouldn’t have chosen that carrier or plan without the iPhone promotion, don’t count the discount as pure savings.

The monthly payment can hide the real commitment

A carrier can reduce the effective monthly cost of an iPhone by offering promotional credits over time. But those credits are generally connected to the financing and promotional terms.

That means the discount isn’t necessarily sitting in my pocket on day one. I’m earning it month after month.

Therefore, if you’re perfectly happy staying with that carrier for the entire promotional period, it can be a very smart way to buy an iPhone. But if you like changing carriers whenever a better deal appears, that “$0 iPhone” doesn’t look quite as free.

Why carrier iPhone deals look almost too good to be true

I’ll give carriers credit here: they know how to make an iPhone promotion look irresistible. For instance, “Get an iPhone for free,” “Get $1,000 off,” or “Get your new iPhone for $X per month.”

Those offers can be real. The catch is that the discount usually comes with conditions. The basic structure is often something like this:

  1. Choose an eligible iPhone.
  2. Trade in an eligible device, if required.
  3. Finance the new iPhone.
  4. Select a qualifying carrier plan.
  5. The carrier applies promotional credits to your bill over time.

The important phrase is “over time.” It’s not an instant discount, which makes switching carriers more complicated.

The biggest advantage of buying an unlocked iPhone is freedom

This is where I think the unlocked iPhone wins decisively. It’s not necessarily the cheapest option. It’s the least complicated option, with the following benefits.

1. Switch carriers whenever you want

This is the biggest advantage for me. If another carrier suddenly offers a better price, coverage, or data plan, I can switch.

This way, you don’t have to calculate how many promotional credits you’re about to lose, ask whether the remaining iPhone balance will become due, or decide whether saving $20 a month on your wireless plan is worth giving up $400 in remaining phone credits.

2. Use a travel eSIM

Apple says that if your iPhone is unlocked, you can use a travel eSIM at your destination. That means I can buy a local or travel eSIM instead of relying entirely on my home carrier’s international roaming option.

Of course, unlocked doesn’t mean universally compatible. The carrier still needs to support the iPhone, its bands, and its eSIM capabilities.

3. Have more freedom when you sell it

This is another advantage I don’t think about until it’s time to upgrade.

An unlocked iPhone is easier to hand to another buyer because the buyer isn’t tied to my old carrier.

4. Control upgrade schedule

I also like not having my upgrade decision dictated by a promotional calendar.

If you want to keep the iPhone for four years, sell it after two years, or find a great trade-in deal next year, you can consider all of these options.

There’s one big downside of an unlocked iPhone

There’s no way around it: An unlocked iPhone can cost you more upfront.

Carrier promotions can be incredibly aggressive because the carrier is using the phone deal to attract or retain customers. If you don’t want that commitment, you may have to give up some of those promotional savings. That’s the trade-off.

I’m essentially choosing between maximum discount and maximum flexibility. For some people, the discount wins. For me, the answer depends on how much flexibility I expect to use.

Want to upgrade early on a carrier deal? You may have to pay off the remaining device balance, lose future credits, or meet specific upgrade conditions. That’s why I always look at the upgrade terms before I call a carrier iPhone “cheap.”

The trade-in trap: Don’t look only at the iPhone discount

This is probably my biggest piece of advice. Don’t get hypnotized by the trade-in number.

A carrier might advertise a huge discount for trading in your current phone. That sounds fantastic. But don’t stop there; compare what you’re actually giving up.

Let’s say my old phone is worth $500 on the private market.

A carrier might advertise a larger promotional credit, but that credit may require me to:

  • Choose a qualifying plan.
  • Finance the new iPhone.
  • Remain with the carrier.
  • Wait months or years to receive the entire promotional amount.

If a carrier’s promotional deal requires you to move from a $50 monthly plan to a $90 plan, don’t pretend that extra $40 doesn’t exist. Over two years, that’s potentially $960 in additional service costs.

Meanwhile, another retailer or Apple might give me a smaller but immediate trade-in credit toward a new iPhone, and I can stay on the same $50 monthly plan. Overall, that can lower the total cost for the way you actually use your phone.

My final verdict: Which one should you buy?

After looking at the price, financing, carrier locks, trade-in promotions, and flexibility, I wouldn’t give everyone the same answer.

Buying through a carrier actually makes more sense if you:

  • Are already happy with the carrier and plan to keep the same plan anyway.
  • Like the coverage and service.
  • Get a strong trade-in promotion.
  • Don’t need to pay significantly more for the required plan.
  • Don’t plan to upgrade early.
  • Pay a genuinely lower total cost than you would by buying the iPhone unlocked.

I would buy the iPhone unlocked instead if you:

  • Switch carriers frequently.
  • Want to use a cheaper mobile plan.
  • Travel internationally and want to use travel eSIMs.
  • Don’t want promotional credits controlling when you can leave.
  • Want to sell the iPhone whenever you choose.
  • Don’t want to commit to a carrier for several years.
  • Value flexibility more than the maximum possible discount.

For me, this is the safer default. Which one are you going for? Let us know in the comments below!

title.rendered: Fortnite’s One Wish Willow Sprite is here: How to find it

content.rendered:
The Fortnite x Obsession collab has finally dropped and, as a result, the One Wish Willow Sprite has become the latest addition to the sprites lineup. This inclusion puts to bed long-running speculations about when this particular crossover with the hit 2025 film, which was first teased back on July 20, would arrive.

One Wish Willow Sprite and Honey Sprite, which rolled out today as well, take the multiplayer game’s unique sprite count to 27. If we count the variants as well, the total number of these critters shoots to a whopping 157, giving the players who are into sprite-hunting some reasonable amount of work to indulge in.

For a quick head start, you can check out the ability and upgrade boosts of the One Wish Willow Sprite in Fortnite. Plus, a few different ways using which you can make the process of catching this sprite seamless are also given below.

One Llama Luck, how may we assist you? https://t.co/H2NGniAHvv

— Fortnite (@Fortnite) July 20, 2026

What the One Wish Willow Sprite does in Fortnite

Similar to any sprite, One Wish Willow Sprite does have its own unique ability, which is to automatically extract the sprites equipped by the player you eliminate in a match. However, unlike other sprites, it also has a secondary ability and another distinct trait that takes inspiration from Obsession’s female lead character Nikki.

While One Wish Willow Sprite’s secondary ability involves pushing everything away when taking damage, its Nikki-esque behavior is basically getting ‘upset’ when unequipped and consequently marking you on the opponents’ map as a punishment for the same. Owing to the latter behavior, it’s the first Fortnite sprite of its kind to not only give the player an advantage but also a disadvantage, depending on whether or not you choose to switch sprites.

Additionally, One Wish Willow Sprite is a Mythic sprite, and it comes in all sprite variants except the Quack variant.

Ways to claim the One Wish Willow Sprite in Fortnite

Activating cheat codes

Given that One Wish Willow Sprite is a Mythic-tier item, it’s best to only target the golden Legendary Cheat Codes and the pink Epic Cheat Codes for eventually extracting this one. You can either use a Cheat Code Locator gizmo to mark a nearby cheat code during a match or simply search locations that have a dense population of these sprite-spawning panels.

Among the best places to look for cheat codes are Heatwave Harbor, Cluster Coast, Shaken Sanctuary, and Sunken Shores. Moreover, if you are looking to stock up on Cheat Code Locators before your visit, you may want to give certain Fortnite Lobby Hacks a try, as some of them provide gizmos of that kind for free.

Locating Pumpkin Chests

Since the introduction of Pumpkin Chests, they have become one of the main ways to obtain sprites in Fortnite Override, arguably only behind Cheat Codes. These Halloween-inspired chests that were rolled out for Fortnitemares 2026 exclusively grant sprites that are related to the horror theme of this ongoing event.

While Pumpkin Chests are not as prevalent in Fortnite Battle Royale as the standard chests are, certain locations that house multiple of these chests do exist. These locations include Nightmare Neighborhood, Freaky Fields, Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria, and Stone Sanctum. Since they aren’t as commonly available, expect competing players to be there when you approach one of these Pumpkin Chest locations.

Hunting for Rare Chests

After Fortnite Runners, Rare Chests have stopped being a likely source of sprites. However, they still have some chance of offering you one, especially if you have the corresponding loot hack unlocked.

For boosting your chances, you can upgrade the Sprite Loot Hack all the way to its maximum spawn rate. On top of that, you can equip a Loot Hacker variant sprite when opening chests, as it increases the chances of one of your loot hack unlocks triggering.

Once you’ve got the aforementioned figured out and are ready to go, you may scour Fortnite map locations with the highest number of Rare Chests. Some of these highly contested areas are Nightmare Neighborhood, Stone Sanctum, the three Pac-Man islands, and the maze to the southeast of Stone Sanctum. Since all the mentioned places are usually swarming with players, it’s best to start chest-hunting only after you have picked up fairly powerful weapons and enough consumables.

Indexing with the help of a friend

As is obvious, an efficient way of adding a new sprite such as the One Wish Willow Sprite into your collection is by temporarily borrowing it from another player. You can find like-minded Fortnite users on the game’s official Discord.

This method requires you and your friend to join two matches together. The first one will involve the other player dropping the sprite for you to pick up and extract. On the other hand, the second match will involve you returning the sprite.

After that, you can go to the Override tab and, from the Sprites section, recall the One Wish Willow Sprite by spending some Sprite Dust. In case you don’t have enough of that, refer to the previously mentioned Lobby Hacks to get some for free.

Wrapping up

One Wish Willow Sprite is certainly an innovation in this particular gameplay aspect of Fortnite. Prior to this, we had never encountered a critter like this that provides a buff but also a sort of de-buff when you decide to ditch it.

That particular element of this Obsession-inspired sprite thoroughly captures the essence of the Inde Navarrette-starrer feature film. Now, it’s only a matter of how many players think that’s enough to make this sprite a popular choice among them.

title.rendered: Apple’s regulatory listing may point to a redesigned iPad mini

content.rendered:
Apple’s French regulatory website has a listing for an unreleased iPad mini Smart Folio case, according to MacRumors, which reported it on October 15. The case carries model number A3632. MacRumors says that number matches no current or past iPad mini case. The listing sits alongside iPhone 18 Pro accessories that Apple added in September, and it has no specs, price, or launch date. Apple has not announced a new iPad mini.

A new case number may mean a new design

Apple’s current iPad mini Smart Folio is sold for the A17 Pro model. MacRumors reads the new number as a sign of a redesign that could make today’s iPad mini cases incompatible. Nothing in the listing confirms the fit, so that question stays open until Apple shows the device.

The OLED link comes from reporting, not the listing

MacRumors says the case could be for the OLED iPad mini that Bloomberg has reported. The listing itself does not mention a display. Today’s 8.3-inch mini uses an LCD panel, and OLED screens can show deeper blacks and higher contrast. MacRumors also lists a more water-resistant design among the rumored details. Earlier, MacRumors matched code identifiers in macOS 26.7 to the same OLED model. Neither piece confirms the screen.

Price and timing come from Bloomberg’s earlier reports

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has said the OLED model will cost considerably more than today’s mini, possibly close to $799. Apple has not set a price for the new model. Apple’s current model starts at $599 for the 128GB Wi-Fi version, after a price increase earlier this year moved it up from $499. At $799, the mini would sit $50 above the 11-inch iPad Air, which starts at $749.

Bloomberg has pointed to a launch on or around October 27, the same window it gives for OLED MacBook Pro models. Before Bloomberg’s October 8 report, MacRumors had called the mini’s timing unclear and placed it in neither of Apple’s two reported October launch waves. Apple’s October 13 press release introduced HomeView, a 7-inch smart home display priced at $299 in the U.S. with sales starting November 13. It did not mention an iPad mini.

What to do if you need a case or a mini now

The current iPad mini starts at $599. Apple’s newsroom and store pages will show the model name, price, and any compatible cases once it announces the device. If you are buying a case for a future mini, wait for that listing, since a changed design could change which cases fit.

  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

title.rendered: Touchscreen MacBook Pro could launch on November 6

content.rendered:
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said on a podcast that Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook Pro could launch on Friday, November 6. MacRumors reported the date on October 15. Apple has not announced the laptop, a date, or a price, so November 6 is a reported possibility.

The same report says Apple is planning to introduce the OLED models on October 27 or 28. It does not explain how that introduction relates to a November 6 launch.

November 6 rests on a podcast remark and a store schedule

Apple’s retail stores apparently have a “big floor reset” scheduled for the evening of Thursday, November 5, running into Friday, November 6. Gurman says that could be preparation for the new Macs. A floor reset shows when stores plan to change their displays. It does not show when a product goes on sale.

Earlier reports pointed to October 27

A Bloomberg report that MacRumors covered on October 8 said Apple would introduce OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro models “on or around” Tuesday, October 27, along with an OLED iPad mini. Bloomberg said the October events would include an online video presentation and a hands-on session for members of the media.

Gurman has also said the laptop could come as early as October and slip to November. He added that Apple is testing the laptops in a macOS 27.2 beta, which he expects to be released toward the end of October.

The reports center on an OLED screen that takes touch

The new models would use OLED screens instead of mini-LED, and the reports describe 14-inch and 16-inch sizes. Touch would work alongside the keyboard and trackpad. Earlier Bloomberg-based reporting described larger touch targets and gestures such as pinch-to-zoom. Reports say macOS 27 may enlarge menus and controls when touch is detected.

Reports also describe a hole-punch camera cutout in place of the notch, paired with a Dynamic Island-style interface.

The OLED models could be sold alongside the current mini-LED MacBook Pro models as a higher-end option, according to the October 15 report. Reports say touch would not reach the MacBook Air at first.

Chip reports conflict, and no price has been reported

The October 15 report says the OLED models would use the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips already in current MacBook Pros. Earlier reports named M6 Pro and M6 Max chips instead.

No price has been reported. Macworld expects a higher starting price because OLED panels cost more to make.

Apple has not confirmed the name, date, or price

Earlier reporting suggested the model could be called the MacBook Ultra, a tier above the MacBook Pro. Bloomberg’s recent reporting puts the 14-inch and 16-inch models in the MacBook Pro family instead. Apple has not said which name it will use.

Earlier reporting put the launch in late 2026 or early 2027, and supply constraints were cited as a reason it could slip into 2027.

The October 15 report includes no Apple statement. An Apple announcement would be the first confirmed source for the date, name, and price. Until then, the reports point to two dates: October 27 or 28, and November 6.

  • Apple HomeView

  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

title.rendered: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816B model that runs on two Mac Studios

content.rendered:
Meta released the weights for Muse Spark Open on October 15. The model has 816 billion parameters, with 42 billion active for each token, and a 1-million-token context window. In its announcement, Meta says the model runs on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios. One Mac Studio cannot hold the whole model.

Two 512GB Mac Studios are needed to hold the model

Each M5 Ultra Mac Studio can give its integrated GPU up to 512GB of unified memory. Meta’s post says the pair works like one machine with about a terabyte of memory, and that the chip’s 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth is fast enough to read the small slice of the model each token needs. The post does not say how the two machines are connected. Apple says Mac Studios can be clustered over Thunderbolt 5.

A smaller model needs far less memory. An Ollama setup runs on a Mac with 8GB of RAM.

Meta says it ran agentic workflows entirely on-device with Muse Code, its coding agent, powered by Muse Spark Open. The tests included iOS fixes and new features for Ice Cubes, an open-source Mastodon client. In a DaVinci Resolve test, the model reviewed footage frame by frame and cropped clips to vertical format.

The 512GB configuration is due in late October

Apple lists $5,499 as the starting price of the M5 Ultra Mac Studio. The 512GB configuration is coming in late October. Meta’s model card puts the NVFP4 version at 700GB of memory, so the two-machine setup likely needs that top option.

The Information reported that demand for local AI hardware pushed Apple’s August refresh forward. Apple has not confirmed that.

A comparison of the M6 Mac mini and M5 Ultra Mac Studio finds the Mac mini the better choice for most people. The Studio suits heavier work such as large-scale AI.

Hugging Face needs a login, and large API resellers need a Meta deal

The weights are on Hugging Face in BF16 and NVFP4 versions. The page asks users to log in and review the conditions before they can access the model. Meta’s model card says running the model on your own system requires at least 700GB of GPU memory for NVFP4 and 2TB for BF16. The card does not say which version the Mac setup uses.

The model ships under the Muse Model License. Meta says its commercial terms are limited and let many developers use the model for free. The license sets a revenue threshold for hosted services. A company that gives third parties API access to the model must sign a separate written agreement with Meta once its combined gross revenue passes $20 million in any 12-month period. Internal use and research are exempt.

Readers without two Mac Studios can use hosted API providers, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter, and Together AI. Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, and Microsoft Foundry Models also offer the weights for download.

Meta’s own numbers put it top on MCP-Atlas but behind some rivals overall

Meta’s model card compares Muse Spark Open with other open-weight models. It scores 39 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, behind Qwen3.8 at 40, Kimi K3 at 44, and GLM 5.3 at 45. It scores 89.2 on MCP-Atlas, a test of agent tool use, the highest score in that table.

Because the weights are open, Meta added extra safety training, and the model met the release thresholds in its Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework. A full evaluation report is “available soon.”

Meta said in April it hoped to open future Muse models

Meta launched Muse Spark in April to power the Meta AI app and meta.ai. The April post said Meta hoped to open-source future versions of the model. The Muse Spark Open model card describes the release as an open-weights version with additional safety post-training. Meta’s announcement does not give a date for the next open release.

  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

Looking for Kaiju Alpha codes? Then you’re in the right place! In order to upgrade your Kaiju and make it as powerful as possible, you’ll need plenty of Tokens and other resources. However, farming these items can prove to be quite challenging, especially if you’re new to the game.

However, there’s no need to worry, as we’ve compiled a list of the active Kaiju Alpha codes that you can redeem for free Tokens and other in-game rewards to speed up your progression.

All working Kaiju Alpha codes

  • PRIME: Free rewards (Play for 15 minutes to redeem) (NEW)
  • HAPPYHALLOWEEN: 31 Levels (Play for 31 minutes to redeem)
  • NOLIMITTOTHELARVA: 20 Levels (Play for 30 minutes to redeem)
  • 1MILLIONMEMBERS: 50 Levels, Cell and Exp boost (lasts 5 hours), and 500k Cells ( Join the group and play for an hour to redeem)

Expired or unverified Kaiju Alpha codes

BADSONGLEE, DEAWYGIGACHAD, KAONTOP, ROSE, SINGULARITY, SRRYFORBUG, SRRYFORBUGGUYS, SRRYFORBUGS, SRRYFORREVERTLEVEL, XECRETISREAL

How to redeem Kaiju Alpha codes in Roblox

Knowing the active codes isn’t enough, gamers! You also need to know how to redeem them and claim your free rewards. Thankfully, the process only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Kaiju Alpha codes:

  1. Fire up Kaiju Alpha on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Click on the Options button.
  4. Paste a working code and hit Enter to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Where to find more Kaiju Alpha codes

The developers don’t follow a fixed schedule for releasing new Kaiju Alpha codes. Most codes are released to celebrate major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Discord server: Visit the Kaiju Alpha Discord server to find announcements and newly released codes.
  • Follow the Roblox game page: Check the game’s official Roblox page for updates, announcements, and potential code releases.
  • Bookmark this page: We’ll update this guide whenever new Kaiju Alpha codes become available, so you can easily find the latest rewards in one place.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Drop a Fruit codes, Anime Dice codes, Turbo Soccer codes and our complete Roblox game codes hub.

FAQs

Why Are My Kaiju Alpha Codes Not Working?

Make sure you’ve entered the code exactly as shown in our list, including the correct spelling, capitalisation, and special characters. If a code still doesn’t work, it may have expired or already been redeemed on your account. You can also try restarting the game and entering the code again.

What Rewards Can You Get From Kaiju Alpha Codes?

Kaiju Alpha codes can give you a variety of rewards such as Cells, EXP boosts, Tokens, and instant levels. These help you to unlock upgrades, level up Kaiju and progress faster.

title.rendered: How to get the Dollie skin in Fortnite | Lost Dolls bundle items list

content.rendered:
Fortnite has been consistently shipping spooky cosmetics into the Item Shop, in line with the Halloween-themed Fortnitemares event, and Dollie is one of the original skins created for this very occasion. In the Lost Dolls category, besides Dollie, there are Mineko and Peppa Pinns as well.

Unlike a chunk of the skins released recently, these cosmetics aren’t the result of any third-party collab but are original designs created by Fortnite devs. Additionally, this is their first stint in the online multiplayer title, having only debuted on October 9.

While the aforementioned three skins can be purchased individually for 1,200 V-Bucks each, you can alternatively grab the Lost Dolls Bundle, which comes with extras, for 2,300 V-Bucks. Moreover, these items are only available in the Shop until October 15, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET.

Steps to claim the Dollie skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Next, scroll down to the Fortnitemares section and select it.
  3. Then, scroll down to the Locker of Horrors category and select your desired skin.
  4. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

All Lost Dolls bundle items in Fortnite

The following cosmetics are all the items that are included in the Lost Dolls Bundle. Their individual prices and respective bundled freebies are also listed below.

1. Dollie

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Doll Eyes wrap

2. Mineko

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Glowing Blossom wrap

3. Pippa Pinns

Price: 1,200 V-Bucks
Also includes: Baneful Blaster wrap

4. Dollie’s Dark Portrait back bling

Price: 300 V-Bucks

5. Baneful Bunbun back bling

Price: 400 V-Bucks

6. Sakura Shamisen pickaxe and back bling

Price: 800 V-Bucks

7. Music Box Mannequin emote

Price: 400 V-Bucks

8. Glowing Blossom wrap

Price: 500 V-Bucks

9. Doll Eyes wrap

Price: 500 V-Bucks

10. Baneful Blaster wrap

Price: 500 V-Bucks

Wrapping up

Fortnitemares 2026 has turned out to be a rather remarkable rendition this time, at least in terms of cosmetics content. From original skins such as Dollie to major third-party collab skins such as Sora (Kingdom Hearts) and Joker (Persona), cosmetic items have come out at a consistent cadence and also feature an intriguing amount of variety among them.

Over the final few weeks of Fortnitemares and Fortnite Override itself, both of which will run till October 31, a few more popular collabs are set to make their way into the Item Shop. This forthcoming lineup features names such as Hazbin Hotel, Obsession, and The Purge. It will be interesting to see how the players, a sizable section of whom have been excitedly awaiting a few of these IPs, receive the content drop once it’s out.

  • How to get the Doja Cat skin in Fortnite
  • How to get the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Lucy skin in Fortnite
  • How to get the Inoxtag skin in Fortnite

  • Razer Naga V3 Pro Gaming Mouse

  • Ergonomic Gaming Chair (Adjustable Lumbar Support)
